sentences.text: Ffion, Yugraj and Jessica say being ghosted has become a common part of applying for jobs Have you ever applied for a job or attended an interview, only to hear absolutely nothing back from the employer?
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: So-called "job ghosting" has become a big problem for jobseekers in the UK, leaving them "demoralised", denting their confidence and undermining their hopes of finding work.
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: It's an issue that was mentioned in former minister Alan Milburn's major review into young people who are not in employment, education or training -  those dubbed as Neets - this week.
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: Among his recommendations - aimed at reducing the proportion of Neets from 13% to about 5% by 2036 - Milburn proposed that large employers should give all unsuccessful job applicants under 25 "meaningful feedback".
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: The report's proposals relate mostly to England, with a recommendation that Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland adapt the principles to suit their own systems.
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: But is feedback for all applicants realistic, given the vast number of applications these firms receive?
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: And what can people do to improve their chances in such a tough job market?
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: Yugraj Samrai, 23, from Coventry is currently unemployed and says he has submitted hundreds of job applications since he graduated from his marketing degree in July.
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: But 30 to 40% of the time he hears nothing back at all, which can make him "feel like a statistic, not a person".
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: He tells the BBC: "I understand there are very few graduate jobs available, but at least give me a response to say whether I'll progress onto the next stage or not." Ffion Johns, from Llanelli, has been unemployed since June and did not get an interview until September after submitting 70 applications.
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: The 24-year-old says her biggest problem throughout the job-hunting process has been the lack of feedback about why she didn't get the job, so she knows what to fix next time.
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: Sometimes she has even been ghosted after attending an interview.
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: "With most of these roles I'm not getting a rejection.
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: I'm just not hearing anything, which can be quite frustrating," she says.
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: Research by head-hunting firm Robert Walters last year found 86% of UK job hunters said their applications had been ignored, with no response at all from the hiring organisation.
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: The Milburn report , external says this "wall of silence" is especially hard on young people as it gives them "nothing to learn from".
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: It adds that "time and emotional investment" goes into their applications.
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: "It can really take hours and hours, so it just feels even worse to not even have that be recognised," says Jessica Anderson, 21, from Swindon.
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: Employers say they are being flooded with job applications in a very competitive jobs market and it can be hard to respond to all of them.
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: And AI is adding to the problem, enabling applicants to submit large numbers of applications in the hope of improving their chances.
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: But Meg Burton, a career coach based in Leeds, says firms should at the very least inform job applicants when they are unsuccessful and that AI could help achieve this.
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: Candidates should also be given proper feedback if they reach the interview stage, she says.
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: "It doesn't have to be hugely detailed, it's just some pointers on why they were unsuccessful and what they can learn from that experience going forward," she says.
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: The government could choose to adopt the Milburn proposals and crack down on job ghosting.
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: But it raises another question: if candidates began receiving significantly more rejections than before, could this itself have a demoralising effect?
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: Ellie McCrone, 20, from Northampton understands the concern but thinks hearing back and getting constructive feedback where possible is always best.
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: Ellie says constructive feedback is always preferable to being ghosted "If you are applying for hundreds of jobs and never getting anything, I think something is going wrong...
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: You can't fix something unless you know what the problem is." There are things applicants can do to improve their chances and avoid ghosting, such as tailoring their CV to each job and not submitting "hundreds and hundreds of applications" that all look the same, Burton adds.
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: Candidates should also never take being ghosted personally, she adds.
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: "Not hearing back doesn't mean you aren't a great candidate.
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: Put it down to experience and move on."
sentences.article_title: Employers are being asked to give interview feedback - here's what applicants want

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Trailer for new programme detailing Princess Catherine's cancer journey The Princess of Wales has spoken about how "cancer does change you," in a forthcoming documentary called Heal to be shown on the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: "It changes your body, it changes you physically - but there is a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you," says Catherine in the first glimpses from the documentary, which features her private thoughts on her illness and recovery.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: "It's clear we're not meant to carry life's challenges alone," says Catherine's voice-over, accompanied by images of other cancer patients and the princess hugging her own family, including Prince William.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: "It is often through pain that we realise there is a greater beauty that lies beyond that," she says, once again reflecting the sense of change from her cancer experience.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: Kensington Palace shared a photo of Catherine doing the Three Peaks Challenge, ahead of the documentary Catherine has never disclosed what type of cancer she faced, but in March 2024 she revealed that she had a diagnosis of cancer and was receiving chemotherapy .
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: In January 2025 she announced that she was in remission and in the following months began a gradual return to royal duties.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: She has often spoken about her different understanding of life after her illness, and the need to take a more holistic approach to well-being beyond physical recovery.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: The princess has talked about the good days and bad days that followed her treatment - and wanted to dispel the idea that patients could immediately return to how they felt before their illness.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: This documentary, which will be introduced by Kirsty Young, promises to be the fullest and most personal account of that journey, with her own insights into the impact such illness can have and how she found her own healing process.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: She has since returned to working for her charities and earlier this week was in India for the Earthshot Prize ceremony with Prince William, the first time they had travelled together on overseas royal duties since the princess's cancer treatment.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: Catherine visited India for William's Earthshot Prize which was hosted in Mumbai - the first time she'd been at the Earthshot awards since 2022 Among the film crew for the documentary, as director of photography, was Will Warr, who has worked with Catherine and her family before.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: His pictures have been used in a video birthday message by Catherine and a Christmas card which showed a relaxed image of the princess and Prince William and their children.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: Catherine was treated at The Royal Marsden Hospital and funds from the distribution of this documentary, which is to be broadcast in other countries, will be paid to The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: When cancer patients finish treatment at the London hospital they can symbolically ring a bell.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Musicians being 'reskinned' by AI copycats Is this real or AI?
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: It is a question increasingly asked underneath social media videos, and often difficult to tell.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: But there is a new trend when it comes to digital manipulation.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Across social media, AI-generated characters are appearing in videos that look remarkably similar to those posted by real people.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: From musicians to dancers and comedians, content creators are finding their performances cloned by these characters that are designed to look funny, realistic, or hypersexualised.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Experts call the practice "reskinning" and say it is made possible by cheap, easy-to-use AI tools.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: People can discover their work has been copied by seeing a video of a character making the same joke or doing the same dance, even with the same background.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Sometimes the AI version has millions more views than the original.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Some of the accounts identified by BBC Verify appear to be using these AI-generated videos to get views and likes, and to eventually make money.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Others appear to be experimenting with AI to make people laugh or simply for the attention that comes with going viral.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: But the practice has angered content creators who say their original work is being stolen.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Lloyd says videos of her performances have been repeatedly reskinned by accounts that replaced her with over-sexualised AI-generated characters.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: One Facebook account published hundreds of short videos of a guitarist called "Mila Vasari" that had each gained thousands of views.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: BBC Verify found that at least three copied Lloyd's performances and used the exact same music, movements, and even facial expressions.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: BBC Verify did not find any evidence that "Mila Vasari" is a real person.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: The videos on the Vasari account also contain visual inconsistencies that suggest AI was used to create them, including distorted fingers playing chords that don't match the music, and guitar strings that fail to move when strummed.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: The account, which appears to be run from Canada, did not respond to questions about the purpose of these videos.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Its profile links to a page devoted to Vasari on Fanvue, a subscription platform that allows creators to charge for content, including adult material.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: BBC Verify has found two other accounts fronted by AI-generated guitarists that have reskinned Lloyd's performances and use those avatars to sell and promote adult content.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: But Lloyd is far from alone in having her content manipulated by AI.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: "I've got so many messages from other artists and creators that have had the same thing happening to them," says Kjetil Krogstad, a Norwegian content creator known for videos showing him happily dancing in a suit while carrying a cup of tea.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: In March, his followers alerted him to the fact that one of his videos had been reskinned using an AI-generated bunny.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: The post went on to attract millions of views - outperforming Krogstad's original video - before being deleted.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: When Krogstad looked into the account behind the bunny video, he found it promoting courses on how to make money from AI-generated content.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Dr Tina Kendall, an expert in online culture at Anglia Ruskin University, says that while these videos are sometimes made for fun, often the people behind the accounts copy videos that have already proven popular in the hope of attracting audiences and making money.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: "What these tools allow people to do is just automatically take a viral concept that's already existing and to reuse it through these reskinning tools," she says.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Kendall sees this as part of a wider online "hustle culture", in which accounts seek to turn users' attention and engagement into money - be it through subscriptions to fan pages featuring adult  content, risky cryptocurrency products like meme coins, or monetisation features on social media platforms.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: And making these copies "conventionally attractive, white, feminine" characters can help, Kendall says.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: "I cannot explain how angry I am right now," Grace Roberts, a British car creator, said on Instagram.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: "I put the videos side by side and I could see it was my exact facial movements, how my body moved, the exact same background and even the people around me were completely copied," she told BBC Verify.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: "It was just me that had been altered." "I pay for the cars, I build the cars, I pay for the cameras, the filming equipment, and then someone can just hit download on their computer, change it, and then make money off the back of my video," she added.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Her concerns are echoed by other content creators who fear these AI-generated accounts could cost them valuable exposure, followers, and potential income.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: American comedian Julia Jasunas, who called out having her jokes stolen online by AI, said in a recent Instagram video: "The thing that is most concerning is these AI bots are going viral and people think that they're real people.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: "And for context, comedians post their stand-up clips online to get you to come out and see live comedy," she said, adding that comedians spent a long time crafting jokes on stage and honing them into punchy lines.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: But legal protections are only part of the challenge.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Identifying those responsible for copying the videos, and stopping them from doing it again, can also prove difficult.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Stopping these pirated performances is a game of whack-a-mole, says Alwyn Cruz, who has made a name for himself on social media by exposing AI musicians.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: "You don't even know who's making these [videos].
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: And then if you shut it down, they're just going to create another," he says.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Earlier this week the head of Instagram, Adam Mosseri, said the platform is also "working quickly on ways to catch copies that are harder to spot, like when someone takes scripts or jokes and uses AI to swap out the visuals".
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: But for artists like Lloyd, the damage may already be done.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: "It takes years to master an instrument and seconds to take and rip it off as something else - and then people don't even know it's you." What do you want BBC Verify to investigate?

sentences.text: According to content creator Richard Cross, social media is a "major player" in raising the profile of today's service stations.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: Dubbed "The Services King", the 28-year-old motoring enthusiast says he has noticed "a shift in the offers we've got on motorway service areas" since an increase in social media coverage.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: "Everybody's had to improve and up their game to cater for those new audiences," he says.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: "I think it taught a lot of people that they want more value for their money, but they also want a better quality product as a result of that." Cross says his own interest in service stations was inspired by his childhood travels with his lorry driver father.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: He has since stopped at all the UK's official motorway service stations, and regularly documents his visits online.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: "There's always a new story to tell within motorway services," he explains.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: Newer sites in particular can cater to new customer expectations, Cross says.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: One of the UK's first motorway service stations was Watford Gap in Northhamptonshire , which opened in 1959, the same day as Newport Pagnell Services.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: Owned by RoadChef, this year it was ranked last in the Transport Focus survey - but still achieved a satisfaction rating of 86%.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: "We are seeing big, airy, open buildings now, letting all that natural light in, and I think we'll continue to see that as they evolve over time," Cross explains.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: "Beforehand, they were catering for a different level of traffic back then, and offering a different set-up as well.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: "Those buildings are now starting to become just a little bit too compact for what modern day expectations are." Like Cross, retail expert Jonathan De Mello, believes the function of motorway service stations is evolving to keep up with a diverse array of demands.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: "You can do a lot more in service stations than you could in the past," he explains.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: "It was just a pit-stop on the way to somewhere else.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: Now it's almost trying to increase dwell times through the presence of a mix of operators [to] facilitate that." De Mello suggests one reason for this could be due to residential housing developments being built further outside cities, with less access to retail offerings.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: Service stations then act as "hubs for local convenience", he says.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: "These service stations become quite good ports of call for certain items, like groceries or health and beauty products.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: "I think people always want the best of everything they can get whenever they do anything, and people's expectations over the years continue to rise," he says.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: Service station providers have to consider multiple factors to match that demand, Diviney explains, such as "the brands that we offer [and] that wi-fi is there if they want to do work emails while the car is charging on site".
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: "And we need to make all that available to them," he adds.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: Welcome Break's CEO John Diviney says service station providers need to consider "multiple factors" to attract visitors A little further along the M1, located outside Leeds, is Skelton Lake services.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: The site, run by Extra, backs onto Skelton Lake Country Park, a popular dog-walking spot.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: Tim and Marie, travelling with their four terriers back to Nottinghamshire from North Yorkshire, say they regularly choose to pause here when travelling.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: "It's a really nice location to stop off," Marie explains.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: "On the way up, we were directed off the motorway so we we had to stop at another one and they're definitely not as dog friendly.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: "This has got this beautiful grassy area so we can walk." If she lived locally, it would be "handy to pop in for some of the outlets they've got", she adds.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: Sitting on a bench overlooking the lake, Wayne and dachshund Fritz are heading home after a holiday in Whitby.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: "We come here every single time we pass," he says.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: "I've done it since it opened because it's probably the best service station for dog walking.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: As soon as we realised it has lakes at the back, we don't go anywhere else." Wayne says he hopes more service stations will develop areas designed for dogs, and their owners, to stretch their legs.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: "There's a lot more dog ownership now.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: If you're walking around a car park, it can actually be quite dangerous with all the cars," he says.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: Marie and Tim chose to stop at Leeds Skelton Lake Services to walk their dogs Looking to the future, more electric vehicles (EVs) on the road could also drive the trend of service stations transforming into leisure destinations, De Mello says.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: According to government data, there are more than two million EVs registered on UK roads, with one in four new cars sold now being fully electric models.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: "People are staying longer because, rather than just filling up the tank with petrol and going on your way, you're sitting there while your car charges," De Mello explains.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: "So having a service station that has more facilities naturally means there are going to be more opportunities to spend." However, Cross says he is "still to be convinced" of the long-term influence an increase in EV vehicle ownership will have on the service station industry.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: He points out that as technology improves, charging times could drop, so operators may not want to "put all their eggs in one basket".
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: Cross predicts the trend for "offline" sites - located on surrounding roads rather than directly off the motorway - could continue.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: "They are more accessible to locals as well as passing traffic, and I think we're going to continue to see that as we get new motorway services because it captures a new market," he says.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: Leeds Skelton Lakes Services has a mixed retail offering and a lakeside walk Cross says his own content has been through an evolution in itself, although his love for the UK's service station scene remains as strong as ever.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: "Before, I was just turning up to sites, taking a couple of photographs and then disappearing.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: "For me, it's such a fascinating perspective to kind of understand and hear," he adds.
sentences.article_title: From pit-stops to go-to destinations: The transformation of service stations

sentences.text: Peter Fluck alongside a satirical puppet of Margaret Thatcher that he created, pictured in 1992 Peter Fluck, co-creator of award-winning satirical puppet show Spitting Image, has died aged 85.
sentences.article_title: Spitting Image co-creator Peter Fluck dies aged 85

sentences.text: His family said he died in the early hours of Saturday at home in Cornwall, following a recent illness.
sentences.article_title: Spitting Image co-creator Peter Fluck dies aged 85

sentences.text: Spitting Image was immensely popular and sometimes controversial, running from 1984-1996 across 18 seasons, and featured puppet caricatures of celebrities, politicians and royals, including former Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher and Queen Elizabeth the Queen Mother.
sentences.article_title: Spitting Image co-creator Peter Fluck dies aged 85

sentences.text: "The spirit that Spitting Image brought to the country was epoch defining," a family statement said.
sentences.article_title: Spitting Image co-creator Peter Fluck dies aged 85

sentences.text: "With Roger Law ('Luck and Flaw'), he brought a unique cutting edge to caricaturing that later evolved into a production company that created the TV series Spitting Image," it added.
sentences.article_title: Spitting Image co-creator Peter Fluck dies aged 85

sentences.text: "Peter's creative life continued after the series for many years from his studio in Cornwall.
sentences.article_title: Spitting Image co-creator Peter Fluck dies aged 85

sentences.text: He was a private man who eschewed fame and attention." The show won several awards, including one Bafta TV award and two Emmys and at its peak drew an audience of 15 million.
sentences.article_title: Spitting Image co-creator Peter Fluck dies aged 85

sentences.text: Fluck was born in Cambridge in 1941, and created the show alongside childhood friend Roger Law, who he met while studying at Cambridge School of Art.
sentences.article_title: Spitting Image co-creator Peter Fluck dies aged 85

sentences.text: Following school, both Fluck and Law moved to London and set up as freelance illustrators, and in 1976 set up their partnership 'Luck and Flaw' back in Cambridge.
sentences.article_title: Spitting Image co-creator Peter Fluck dies aged 85

sentences.text: Peter Fluck (left) and Roger Law in 1984 "You could say we took the traditional newspaper editorial cartoon and put it on the screen," Fluck told ArtCornwall in an interview , external in 2006.
sentences.article_title: Spitting Image co-creator Peter Fluck dies aged 85

sentences.text: He described the show as being shown "at the difficult time of 10 o'clock on a Sunday night when all politicians should have been in bed".
sentences.article_title: Spitting Image co-creator Peter Fluck dies aged 85

sentences.text: Many of the characters included parodies of Thatcher's cabinet, with Douglas Hurd depicted with "Mr Whippy ice cream" hair, and her successor John Major caricatured as a dull, grey puppet with a penchant for peas.
sentences.article_title: Spitting Image co-creator Peter Fluck dies aged 85

sentences.text: "We did get quite a lot of approaches from politicians for their puppet to be made, because if you didn't appear as a puppet on Spitting Image you hadn't made it as a politician," Fluck said in an interview in 2011. , external It was eventually axed by ITV because of declining audience numbers.
sentences.article_title: Spitting Image co-creator Peter Fluck dies aged 85

sentences.text: In a statement, the broadcaster said Fluck's "creative contribution to TV satire is simply unrivalled... his cutting edge puppetry and caricature skills, alongside the show's sharp and always shrewdly observed humour, became a defining part of the cultural zeitgeist.
sentences.article_title: Spitting Image co-creator Peter Fluck dies aged 85

sentences.text: "Our thoughts and deepest sympathies are with his family and friends at this very sad time." When he stepped away from the show, Fluck moved to Cornwall and focused his art on ceramics, printmaking and mobiles.
sentences.article_title: Spitting Image co-creator Peter Fluck dies aged 85

sentences.text: In 2018, Law donated his entire archive of Spitting Images to Cambridge University.
sentences.article_title: Spitting Image co-creator Peter Fluck dies aged 85

sentences.text: The collection - including original scripts, puppet moulds, drawings and recordings - was conserved and held in the library.
sentences.article_title: Spitting Image co-creator Peter Fluck dies aged 85

sentences.text: Penny has a congenital heart condition which affects about five in every 10,000 babies A baby girl is "thriving" after a life-saving operation by surgeons who used a 3D-printed model of her heart to prepare.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: Thirteen-month-old Penny has a congenital heart condition which affects about five in every 10,000 babies, called Tetralogy of Fallot. , external She underwent open-heart surgery at Birmingham Children's Hospital, where her parents faced an agonising wait for news until their daughter came round.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: "All of a sudden she had a twinkle in her eye," said her father, Brad.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: "The anaesthetic was getting out of her system and she was back.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: She was Penny again." The BBC has followed Penny's journey, as her family and doctors prepared for the procedure with the aid of the printed replica of her heart, which helped build a picture of exactly what needed to be done.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: Penny pictured in January as her parents prepared for her operation.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: Earlier this year, Penny's parents Brad and Lizzie found it understandably tough to imagine just what their baby daughter was about to face.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: On the outside she looked healthy, but without surgery she could become gravely ill.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: One was the actual size of her heart and was used to show Brad and Lizzie what surgeons were dealing with, while another, larger and more detailed model was produced for doctors.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: Dr Tristan Ramcharan, a consultant paediatric cardiologist, with Penny, her parents and the 3D heart "Having the replica means that we can see exactly what a heart condition looks like," Dr Tristan Ramcharan, a consultant paediatric cardiologist, explained.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: "Before we go into theatre, we can have a look and see where a hole is, we can see where the narrowing is and, in select and more complicated cases, we can use that to understand exactly where our patches have to go and where we have to cut.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: "It then makes the actual operation easier, more straightforward and potentially less complicated." The model helped Penny's parents understand more about the procedure too.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: But weeks before the operation, during a visit to see the 3D heart for the first time, they were understandably worried.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: "I can't wait to be on the other side," said Lizzie.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: "It's just a day that's looming over us.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: But we know it's got to happen.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: It's something that Penny needs, so, yeah, we are a bit anxious." Antonio Fratini in the health research centre where the 3D heart was made Using CT scans, biomedical engineers worked closely with doctors to ensure the four defects in Penny's heart were accurately represented.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: The partnership between Aston University and nearby Birmingham Children's Hospital uses technology to help both parents and doctors better understand complex heart conditions.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: The team has now produced 3D-printed models of a number of infants' hearts.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: The project is run by the cardiology team at Birmingham Children's Hospital, in conjunction with Aston University, and is funded by the hospital's charity.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: Antonio Fratini, from the university's Engineering for Health Research Centre, said: "Surgeons sometimes tell us which side of the heart they want to see and which areas are of particular interest.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: We don't print the whole heart every time.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: "Sometimes they also ask us to make cuts in the model so they can open it up and see inside." Penny shortly before being taken to the operating theatre Weeks later, an anxious Brad and Lizzie waited at Birmingham Children's Hospital for their daughter to be taken to the operating theatre.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: It was early in the morning and only just getting light.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: Holding his daughter in his arms, Brad said he was "apprehensive and nervous".
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: "Because what she has is hidden, it's very difficult to understand that it is life threatening and it needs to happen.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: But I did have a moment last night thinking actually I could just run away and I felt like protecting her, but the logical part says no this has got to be done." Soon afterwards the couple carried Penny to the operating suite alongside a nurse, and were allowed to be with her until she'd had general anaesthetic.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: "I just crumbled," admitted Brad afterwards.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: "I thought I was here to support Penny and Lizzie, and all of a sudden Lizzie was supporting me." Penny asleep in the days after her operation with her father, Brad The couple then faced an agonising five-and-a-half hour wait for news.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: When the news came, it was positive.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: The operation had been a success.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: But seeing Penny in intensive care was difficult at first.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: She initially had an "external pacemaker", explained Brad.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: "She needed support when she came out," he said, but was "reassured" by staff.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: Penny's parents were finally able to hold her six days later.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: "I took great pleasure in that," said Brad.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: In the coming weeks she will have further checks using a heart monitor and eventually, be checked annually for the rest of her life.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: But generally, the outlook for Penny is now bright.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: "We're delighted that Penny is recovering so well following her surgery.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: Penny and her family have shown incredible bravery throughout, and it's wonderful to see them able to look forward to the future," Ramcharan said.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: Penny after she came out of intensive care.
sentences.article_title: Baby thriving after 3D-printed model used to save her heart

sentences.text: Stalkers may use social media to monitor or repeatedly contact their victims Parents are being urged to recognise the signs of online stalking, amid concerns technology is making it easier than ever for perpetrators to monitor and repeatedly contact young people.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: Experts say persistent unwanted contact, attempts to bypass blocks by creating new accounts and efforts to track someone's online activity can all be early indicators of stalking behaviour.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: Their advice follows the case of a Wiltshire teenager who became "obsessed" with a girl after a five-day relationship, monitoring her online activity and creating fake social media accounts after she blocked him before later attacking her with a knife.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: It also comes as stalking offences have risen across Avon and Somerset, with police recording 1,348 offences last year, up from 954 two years earlier.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: In response to the increase, officers are receiving additional training to help identify stalking behaviour, patterns of control and links to other offences.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: Gloucester Crown Court heard the 14-year-old boy had become "obsessed" with the girl after she ended their relationship.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: The victim's mother told the BBC: "She had no idea that he was logging when she was online, who she was speaking to, what she was saying.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: "There were diaries found in his house [detailing her online activity].
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: It makes me feel sick." The court heard the boy created numerous fake social media accounts to contact the victim after she blocked him, before later attacking her with a 6in knife.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: He admitted wounding with intent, inflicting grievous bodily harm and possession of a bladed article in a public place, but avoided a custodial sentence .
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: "This is something you watch happen to other people and you're horrified by it.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: But now this is my life, and that happened to my child," the victim's mother added.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: The boy unleashed the "vicious" attack in broad daylight and in front of witnesses Police guidance , external describes stalking as repeated, unwanted behaviour that is fixated or obsessive and affects a person's daily life.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: While many people associate stalking with being followed in public, experts say it can increasingly take place online through social media platforms, messaging apps and gaming services.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: Researchers have suggested tools including GPS trackers , social media, home surveillance systems and smartphone apps may be contributing to a wider rise in stalking cases, making it easier for perpetrators to monitor victims remotely.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: Trowbridge-based stalking charity FearFree said concerns should not be dismissed, even when behaviours appear minor at first.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: "We know that sometimes - particularly when the behaviour first starts - it can be hard to recognise the risk it might pose, but it is important to not dismiss your concerns," a spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: "Evidence shows us that stalking is a high-risk behaviour, which can lead to serious violence." Research by the University of Gloucestershire and the Suzy Lamplugh Trust found 94% of murders examined featured prior stalking behaviour.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: Campaigners say concerns about recognising stalking behaviours early have been raised nationally for years, with high-profile cases highlighting the dangers of warning signs being overlooked.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: Police say stalking is often characterised by a pattern of unwanted behaviour rather than a single incident.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: Warning signs can include somebody continuing to send messages after being asked to stop, creating new accounts after being blocked, or keeping track of when a person is online and who they are speaking to.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: Other behaviours can include attempting to infiltrate friendship groups, turning up unexpectedly at places a person regularly visits, sending unwanted gifts or communications, or spreading rumours about them.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: In some cases, stalkers may also try to gain access to email, social media or other online accounts to monitor a victim's activity.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: Although blocking a stalker may seem the obvious response, Gloucestershire-based charity the Hollie Gazzard Trust warns that obsessed perpetrators may be "more likely to physically come round and find you".
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: Instead, Gloucestershire Constabulary advises victims to keep contact with the stalker to a minimum.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: "Blocking can result in a stalker changing their behaviour, which in turn escalates the risk of violence," a spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: The force says previous messages, posts and records of unwanted contact can provide important evidence about the volume and nature of the behaviour.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: "However, we also understand how distressing it can be when you are the victim of this type of behaviour," the force continued.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: However, police stress victims do not need evidence before making contact, although information such as dates, times and witness details can help investigators.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: Personal safety charity the Suzy Lamplugh Trust offers online resources for tracking and recording stalking behaviours , external .
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: "Anything you've got like that can be useful to us, but don't delay reporting to get it," Wiltshire Police advises.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: "Your information could help us bring the offender to justice and make sure you, and other people in a similar situation, are kept safe." Once a report is made, police will assess whether an offence has been committed, how serious the behaviour is and whether the victim is at immediate risk.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: If there are viable lines of enquiry, an investigating officer will usually be assigned and the case may then be referred for further action, including criminal prosecution.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: Stalking carries a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison, and a Stalking Protection Order (SPO) , external can also be enforced to protect a victim of any age.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: The conditions of the order could include prohibiting the stalker from entering certain locations, approaching or contacting the victim, making direct or indirect references to the victim on social media, recording images of the victim, and more.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: Breaching an SPO is deemed a criminal offence under the Stalking Protection Act 2019, and could carry a maximum sentence of up to five years in prison.
sentences.article_title: Parents urged to spot online stalking warning signs as cases rise

sentences.text: The Titanic sank after striking an iceberg in the North Atlantic on 15 April 1912 Rare items belonging to passengers of the Titanic have been sold at auction for record-breaking sums.
sentences.article_title: Rare Titanic items sell for record-breaking sums

sentences.text: The highest selling artefacts were a pocket watch from third-class passenger Mary Mangan, which fetched £250,000, and a diamond ring worn by famous passenger Lady Duff Gordon, which was bought for £140,000.
sentences.article_title: Rare Titanic items sell for record-breaking sums

sentences.text: Another item was a detailed, water-stained letter recovered from the body of its writer, first-class passenger Ramon Artagaveytia Gomez, which was auctioned for £80,000.
sentences.article_title: Rare Titanic items sell for record-breaking sums

sentences.text: Auctioneer Andrew Aldridge from Henry Aldridge and Son in Devizes, Wiltshire, said the "epic sale" was evidence of the lasting global interest in the tragic story.

sentences.text: Why women have rallied behind rape victim Joanne Young Warning about scammers posing as detectives 'Replenished reservoirs' and 'landmark cases' The Titanic departed on its maiden voyage on 10 April 1912 and sank in the early hours of 15 April with the loss of about 1,500 lives.

sentences.text: The golden watch was found on the body of 32-year-old Irish passenger Mangan, and was returned to her family alongside her other possessions.
sentences.article_title: Rare Titanic items sell for record-breaking sums

sentences.text: It has recently spent several weeks on exhibition alongside the rest of the Mangan Collection at Titanic Belfast.
sentences.article_title: Rare Titanic items sell for record-breaking sums

sentences.text: Another was a postcard written by Jack Phillips , a senior wireless operator who died in the disaster after heroic actions.

sentences.text: Phillips remained at his post sending wireless distress calls and helped to coordinate rescue efforts as the ship went down.
sentences.article_title: Rare Titanic items sell for record-breaking sums

sentences.text: The postcard, which was written four days earlier to his sister Elsie, was sold for nearly £32,000.
sentences.article_title: Rare Titanic items sell for record-breaking sums

sentences.text: The auctioneer said the postcard was particularly significant as it was written while the Titanic was docked in Southampton "The sale total was well over £1m and Titanic items made up a large part of that," Aldridge said.

sentences.text: He said the watch broke the record for an item sold from a third-class passenger, while the ring was sold for the highest amount ever for a piece of jewellery from the Titanic "The interest in the story is global, my clients come form all four corners of the world," he said.

sentences.text: Non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) signed by staff at the UK's information watchdog will be lifted to allow them to speak out about its culture, the government has confirmed.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: Ministers are expected to publish the details of how an independent review of the working environment at the Information Commission will be carried out next week.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: It follows the departure of the watchdog's boss five months ago amid allegations of sexually inappropriate behaviour.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: A government spokesperson confirmed that NDAs, known as "gagging clauses", would not be enforced by the Information Commission, saying the regulator "will not use the terms of any agreement to prevent people from participating in the review".
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: The government "will set out further details on the review, including its terms of reference and the independent reviewer, shortly", they added.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: The Information Commission is one of the UK's most high-profile regulators charged with the crucial task of regulating AI, data protection and Freedom of Information requests.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: It recently won a court battle with TikTok after it fined the social media platform £12.7m for misusing children's data, and has penalised bodies including the Ministry of Defence after an email blunder exposed the details of interpreters fleeing Afghanistan.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: But it has been without permanent leadership since Information Commissioner John Edwards resigned earlier this year .
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: It came after an independent investigation found a "case to answer" over reports of alleged inappropriate behaviour towards staff including claims of sexual harassment.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: The Information Commission said the investigation found Edwards' behaviour "fell short of the conduct expected from a public official".
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: In a resignation statement posted on his LinkedIn page in June, Edwards said he disagreed with how the investigation had been carried out but accepted his position had "become untenable".
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: Nine of those , external included a "non-derogatory clause" which legally prevents employees from making negative comments publicly.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: While this is a small proportion of the more than 1,000 staff employed by the commissioner, government advice stipulates that public bodies should only use confidentiality clauses "when necessary" and that they should "not seek to stifle or discourage staff from raising concerns".
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: Since 2025, new laws also mean they cannot be used to silence employees subjected to harassment or abuse.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: Five months later, the investigation has not begun.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: In recent weeks, the two major civil service unions, the PCS and FDA, have pushed for an external examination of the events leading up to Edwards' resignation in meetings with government officials.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: The unions have also asked for those who signed non-disclosure agreements with the ICO to be released from them so they can contribute to the review.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: The PCS union says other concerns had previously been raised with them about Edwards, including a bullying complaint, which was investigated at the time.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: An internal staff survey, published in August and released under FOI , external points towards wider issues at the Commission, with 14% of all employees reporting they had either personally experienced bullying, harassment and discrimination.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: Multiple current and former employees have also told the BBC of experiencing or witnessing incidents of bullying or harassment.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: PCS General Secretary Fran Heathcote said the union's members at the Commission "have been failed for too long by a toxic leadership culture that has allowed bullying and harassment to persist, leaving many staff fearful of speaking out".
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: Heathcote said she welcomed the "positive engagement" the union had received in recent weeks from the Commission and officials at the Department for Culture Media and Sport (DCMS), which oversees it.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: "Instead, a leadership vacuum has compounded what went before at a rudderless organisation where it seems the worst behaviours in the workplace are not being challenged," she added.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: She said it was "vital" the government brought in "someone who can set a new tone and is dedicated to changing attitudes and protecting staff" to head up the Commission.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: A spokesperson for the Information Commission said its commitment to an independent review reflected its "ongoing commitment to listening and learning from the events of the past year and those leading up to it".
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: "Our new Board, appointed this summer, has been working exceptionally hard to provide fresh leadership, ushering in a new governance structure and a new strategy," they added.
sentences.article_title: Staff gagging clauses lifted ahead of probe into culture at data watchdog

sentences.text: Joseph Langdon was supported by the Bristol Old Vic while in a young offenders' institution A former young offender who became a West End actor says taking drama lessons while he was detained was the best decision he ever made.
sentences.article_title: Man who studied drama in young offenders' institution now a West End actor

sentences.text: Joseph Langdon, who grew up in south London, was convicted of gang-related crimes at the the age of 16.
sentences.article_title: Man who studied drama in young offenders' institution now a West End actor

sentences.text: But while in a young offenders' institution, he was offered drama lessons through a scheme with the Bristol Old Vic.
sentences.article_title: Man who studied drama in young offenders' institution now a West End actor

sentences.text: Langdon said the lessons taught him "that I could make something of my life, and introduced me to this world I did not think was possible".
sentences.article_title: Man who studied drama in young offenders' institution now a West End actor

sentences.text: The actor, who will play the prince in the theatre's Christmas production of Cinderella: A Fairytale, said: "I count my blessings every day.
sentences.article_title: Man who studied drama in young offenders' institution now a West End actor

sentences.text: I turn up to rehearsals with a huge smile on my face." "I'm now working all over the world and have the most amazing life," he added.
sentences.article_title: Man who studied drama in young offenders' institution now a West End actor

sentences.text: "At first I was like, 'No I'm not going to go, I feel a bit too cool for this'.
sentences.article_title: Man who studied drama in young offenders' institution now a West End actor

sentences.text: "But when I did decide to go it was the best decision I ever made.
sentences.article_title: Man who studied drama in young offenders' institution now a West End actor

sentences.text: I never skipped a lesson," he said.
sentences.article_title: Man who studied drama in young offenders' institution now a West End actor

sentences.text: At the end of his sentence, Langdon was told he could either move back to London and "get caught up in the same trouble" or move to Bristol "and start life afresh".
sentences.article_title: Man who studied drama in young offenders' institution now a West End actor

sentences.text: The cast of Cinderella have been rehearsing at the Bristol Old Vic Langdon moved to Bristol, where he lived in youth hostels and halfway houses while training at the Old Vic through the Made in Bristol scheme - a free programme for young theatre makers.
sentences.article_title: Man who studied drama in young offenders' institution now a West End actor

sentences.text: He said coming out of prison was tough, but his support network kept him "on track".
sentences.article_title: Man who studied drama in young offenders' institution now a West End actor

sentences.text: The actor also worked at the theatre's box office and took part in various productions before returning to south London to study at Mountview drama school, thanks to a bursary scheme.
sentences.article_title: Man who studied drama in young offenders' institution now a West End actor

sentences.text: He said he was anxious about going back to the area he grew up in but "everybody was so supportive and proud".
sentences.article_title: Man who studied drama in young offenders' institution now a West End actor

sentences.text: After graduating, Langdon went on to act in numerous films and productions, including in the West End.
sentences.article_title: Man who studied drama in young offenders' institution now a West End actor

sentences.text: "I pinch myself every day," he said.
sentences.article_title: Man who studied drama in young offenders' institution now a West End actor

sentences.text: "Being adopted by Bristol has been the biggest blessing of my life," said Langdon, who returns to the city to star in Cinderella.
sentences.article_title: Man who studied drama in young offenders' institution now a West End actor

sentences.text: "The Bristol Old Vic has such a special, special, magical energy" and it is "truly an honour and a blessing to be part of that," said the actor.
sentences.article_title: Man who studied drama in young offenders' institution now a West End actor

sentences.text: Lucy Hunt, Bristol Old Vic's director of engagement, said Langdon understood "first-hand how a bit of belief in a young person can make a big impact on their lives".
sentences.article_title: Man who studied drama in young offenders' institution now a West End actor

sentences.text: "I am so happy he is back," said Hunt.
sentences.article_title: Man who studied drama in young offenders' institution now a West End actor

sentences.text: "Ultimately, it's a beautiful family show full of fun, magic and wonder," said Langdon.
sentences.article_title: Man who studied drama in young offenders' institution now a West End actor

sentences.text: Langdon now goes into schools and gives talks to "be that representation" for those interested in theatre.
sentences.article_title: Man who studied drama in young offenders' institution now a West End actor

sentences.text: He says he wants to "show other people from all different backgrounds, no matter who you are, that this is possible".
sentences.article_title: Man who studied drama in young offenders' institution now a West End actor

sentences.text: Barbara Scott, who has taken comfort from her son's final act, also plans to leave her body to medical science Fifteen years ago Barbara Scott signed documents to leave her body to medical science.
sentences.article_title: My son donated his body to science and became a 'silent teacher'

sentences.text: Her son Oliver McNeil Scott liked the idea and five years ago he also signed up to the body donation programme.
sentences.article_title: My son donated his body to science and became a 'silent teacher'

sentences.text: Barbara, from Lenzie in East Dunbartonshire, never thought her son would go before her - but in April 2025, Oliver died from colorectal cancer at the age of 48.
sentences.article_title: My son donated his body to science and became a 'silent teacher'

sentences.text: His body was signed over to the University of Edinburgh's medical school.
sentences.article_title: My son donated his body to science and became a 'silent teacher'

sentences.text: Despite not having a funeral for her son, Barbara has taken great comfort in his last act.
sentences.article_title: My son donated his body to science and became a 'silent teacher'

sentences.text: Known by those in the medical profession as silent teachers, every body donor contributes to the education of more than 1,000 anatomy students at the university every year.
sentences.article_title: My son donated his body to science and became a 'silent teacher'

sentences.text: Oliver, who was a regular marathon runner, had Ramsay Hunt syndrome, a rare neurological disorder caused by the same virus that results in chickenpox and shingles and affects facial nerves.
sentences.article_title: My son donated his body to science and became a 'silent teacher'

sentences.text: Barbara said being diagnosed with colorectal cancer only added to his determination to combat illness.
sentences.article_title: My son donated his body to science and became a 'silent teacher'

sentences.text: "He always wanted to do the best he could, and even during his illness, he researched all the new cures," Barbara said.
sentences.article_title: My son donated his body to science and became a 'silent teacher'

sentences.text: "In the end, he was going to be receiving a drug from America that he actually found himself, but unfortunately it was too late for Oliver.
sentences.article_title: My son donated his body to science and became a 'silent teacher'

sentences.text: Anatomy bequest co-ordinator Laura Shiels and her team of technicians work to ensure that every individual who gifts their body is cared for with dignity and respect.
sentences.article_title: My son donated his body to science and became a 'silent teacher'

sentences.text: "After Oliver died, it was really quite a shock to us," Barbara said.
sentences.article_title: My son donated his body to science and became a 'silent teacher'

sentences.text: "But when Laura took this on and explained to us all what was going to happen with Oliver, it was so nice." Since Oliver's body arrived at the medical school in April 2025, Barbara has frequently visited the anatomy department so she can feel close to her son.
sentences.article_title: My son donated his body to science and became a 'silent teacher'

sentences.text: "It's just a lovely thing to sit here and think about him and about what a special thing he's done," she said.
sentences.article_title: My son donated his body to science and became a 'silent teacher'

sentences.text: "For Oliver, it is really life after death because he is facilitating students to find out more in the future about what's happened to him, how they can move forward.
sentences.article_title: My son donated his body to science and became a 'silent teacher'

sentences.text: It's really, really important." The University of Edinburgh is one of five universities in Scotland that receives body donations for medical education.
sentences.article_title: My son donated his body to science and became a 'silent teacher'

sentences.text: In the past five years there have been 200 people taken into their care at the end of life and there are currently 4,000 who have signed up.
sentences.article_title: My son donated his body to science and became a 'silent teacher'

sentences.text: The bodies are donated to the university's anatomy department The anatomy department can keep donated bodies for three years.
sentences.article_title: My son donated his body to science and became a 'silent teacher'

sentences.text: Laura says they are vital in helping medical and biomedical students learn about the human body.
sentences.article_title: My son donated his body to science and became a 'silent teacher'

sentences.text: Tom Gillingwater, head of the department, believes body donors are possibly the most important people in the department.
sentences.article_title: My son donated his body to science and became a 'silent teacher'

sentences.text: "The only way that someone could properly have that experiential engagement with what lies inside the body, with what is the true anatomy of the body, is if they are able to look at, touch, and engage with a real body," he said.
sentences.article_title: My son donated his body to science and became a 'silent teacher'

sentences.text: "And when we want to do that looking underneath the skin, the only way we can do it is with someone who's willing to give us their body, where we can cut through that skin and look underneath it.
sentences.article_title: My son donated his body to science and became a 'silent teacher'

sentences.text: These are our silent teachers." The silent teachers also help practising surgeons, some from overseas, to pioneer new medical procedures.
sentences.article_title: My son donated his body to science and became a 'silent teacher'

sentences.text: Laura helps to care for donor families as they come to terms with loss and their relative's decision to leave their body to medical science.
sentences.article_title: My son donated his body to science and became a 'silent teacher'

sentences.article_title: My son donated his body to science and became a 'silent teacher'
