sentences.text: Sophie Hope's credit score was hit by identity fraud Getting approval for a mortgage, a car loan or even a mobile phone contract can rest on a credit score.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Sophie Hope was on the sharp end of just such a decision.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "When I first checked my credit score, it was excellent.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: But then my mortgage application was suddenly denied by the lender because of my credit report.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: It was a massive shock as I'd never had bad credit.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: When I looked into it, my score had gone to 'very poor'," she says.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: It turns out, the Brighton-based nail technician and content creator, had been the victim of identity fraud.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "Someone had opened accounts in my name across various catalogue sites and ordered multiple items, including a PlayStation 4 and Nike socks," she says.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "Without me knowing, the debt was transferred to a secondary finance company.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: It spent three to four years accumulating in the background.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: It was only when I went to apply for a mortgage that I discovered how severely it had dragged down my credit score," she says.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Credit scores are "backward looking" says Funmi Olufunwa Hope's experience shows how crucial a credit score can be, but, as in her case, it does not tell the full story.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "As a nation, we are overly obsessed with credit scores," says Funmi Olufunwa, a consumer finance lawyer and founder of financial education business, Hoops Finance.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Three firms - Experian, Equifax and TransUnion - produce credit scores in the UK, and they all work from roughly the same data.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "A credit score is backward looking.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: It's looking at what has happened in the past, which doesn't necessarily predict the future," says Olufunwa.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "But when somebody's looking to lend you money, they're looking at what actually is affordable," she says.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Traditional credit scoring systems also disadvantage "thin-file applicants" - young people and recent immigrants to the UK who won't have built up a credit history.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: But with more financial data available than ever before - and a growing appetite for AI to make sense of it - could artificial intelligence help lenders work out who is safe to lend to?
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: In the US lending decisions will often hinge on a credit score from a company called FICO, which uses data from the big three credit assessment firms.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: But AI-powered lending firms, Upstart and Zest AI have both built businesses which offer lenders an extra option when it comes to assessing a client's credit worthiness.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "Thanks to our machine-learning models that look at more than 2,500 variables, we believe we can make significantly more loans at low prices to borrowers from every demographic group," Upstart said in statement.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: But like with many other applications of AI into everyday life, there are concerns.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "Consumers need to understand what information is being used to make decisions about them, and they need to be able to challenge something when it is wrong," Tucker explains.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: Credit scores have been a contentious topic for decades for this very reason, says Sandra Wachter, professor of Technology and Regulation at the University of Oxford.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: "We are not assessing if past decisions were right," Wachter argues, adding, AI does not know about existing social inequalities that impact decisions and could just "replicate what it has seen in the past".
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: While companies like Upstart and Zest AI see technology as a tool for financial inclusion, Wachter believes that real transformation requires accountability, as well as automation.
sentences.article_title: Should AI be judging our credit worthiness?

sentences.text: She stresses that firms must apply existing regulations and establish new guardrails to ensure that AI does not simply perpetuate the biases of the past.

sentences.text: Retail sales rose in October, driven by people buying long-life food such as tinned goods and UHT milk, according to official figures.
sentences.article_title: Tinned food and long-life milk boost retail sales after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

sentences.text: Sales volumes were 0.7% higher as people responded to the government's emergency preparedness "Be Ready" campaign, the Office for National Statistics (ONS) said.
sentences.article_title: Tinned food and long-life milk boost retail sales after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

sentences.text: The campaign encouraged people to stock up in case of disruption to essential services by severe weather or cyberattacks.
sentences.article_title: Tinned food and long-life milk boost retail sales after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

sentences.text: Separate research released last week suggested that while households were stockpiling essentials, they were not panic buying .
sentences.article_title: Tinned food and long-life milk boost retail sales after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

sentences.text: The government campaign encouraged people to keep three days' worth of food and water in their homes.
sentences.article_title: Tinned food and long-life milk boost retail sales after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

sentences.text: Wet wipes, a torch and cash were also recommended.
sentences.article_title: Tinned food and long-life milk boost retail sales after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

sentences.text: Data from retail research firm Worldpanel by Numerator indicated last week that  people were stocking up on items including tinned meat, bottled water and hand sanitiser.
sentences.article_title: Tinned food and long-life milk boost retail sales after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

sentences.text: The latest official sales figures , external from the ONS add to the evidence that the public has begun stockpiling.
sentences.article_title: Tinned food and long-life milk boost retail sales after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

sentences.text: "Supermarkets have told us that sales of long-life food items such as tinned food and UHT milk were boosted by the government's 'Be Ready' campaign," ONS chief economist Grant Fitzner said.
sentences.article_title: Tinned food and long-life milk boost retail sales after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

sentences.text: "Meanwhile fuel sales have been recovering from earlier low levels, despite pump prices rising again." The rise in retail sales last month beat some economists' expectations - they had predicted a slight fall - and the increase came after a 0.6% decline in September.
sentences.article_title: Tinned food and long-life milk boost retail sales after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

sentences.text: As well as sales being boosted by people buying essentials, visits to art galleries and clothing purchases were also higher in October.
sentences.article_title: Tinned food and long-life milk boost retail sales after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

sentences.text: The boost in sales comes at the beginning of the festive period, which is normally the busiest time of the year for retailers.
sentences.article_title: Tinned food and long-life milk boost retail sales after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

sentences.text: Jacqui Baker, partner and head of retail at auditing firm RSM UK, said that "retailers will want to see out the year with some Christmas cheer before consumers batten down the hatches in the New Year as energy costs skyrocket and inflation ramps up further".
sentences.article_title: Tinned food and long-life milk boost retail sales after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

sentences.text: Typical energy bills are forecast to go up by £443 per year from January, pushing up the pace of price rises.

sentences.text: Borrowing - the difference between public sector spending and income - was £17bn last month, the ONS said. , external Although that was £0.8bn higher than October last year, it was below analysts' forecasts of about £18bn.
sentences.article_title: Tinned food and long-life milk boost retail sales after 'Be Ready' campaign launch

sentences.text: New rules on what Airbnb hosts can reasonably ask guests to do have come into force.
sentences.article_title: Airbnb's divisive new house rules come into force

sentences.text: Hosts should now not normally ask guests to wash up, for example, but can appeal to Airbnb if they have a compelling reason.
sentences.article_title: Airbnb's divisive new house rules come into force

sentences.text: Some guests have found lists of house rules laborious to complete, with one telling the BBC "it was not relaxing at all".
sentences.article_title: Airbnb's divisive new house rules come into force

sentences.text: But some hosts have said that the costs of paying for extra cleaning may have to be passed on to customers.

sentences.text: The new Airbnb rules, announced last month , allow hosts to choose from seven standard house rules, which include determining how many people can stay overnight, and whether or not pets or smoking are allowed.
sentences.article_title: Airbnb's divisive new house rules come into force

sentences.text: Hosts can then set additional rules, but guests shouldn't be asked to do the washing up, remove sheets from beds, take rubbish out or avoid using utilities.
sentences.article_title: Airbnb's divisive new house rules come into force

sentences.text: Airbnb has begun reviewing listings and will be sending emails to hosts , external "who need to take action" it said.
sentences.article_title: Airbnb's divisive new house rules come into force

sentences.text: Hosts can appeal to Airbnb to argue an additional house rule is necessary, and ask Airbnb to approve it.
sentences.article_title: Airbnb's divisive new house rules come into force

sentences.text: If the house rule is not approved and the host keeps it anyway, Airbnb will flag this to guests on the host's listing page with a message such as "includes cleaning tasks".
sentences.article_title: Airbnb's divisive new house rules come into force

sentences.text: Airbnb said chores can make customers hesitate about booking through the platform, arguing that making house rules "clearer" would increase the number of clients.
sentences.article_title: Airbnb's divisive new house rules come into force

sentences.text: Many of the companies marketing supported housing investments were linked to developer Lee Jones "This building is hell on Earth," says Phil, describing the black mould and rats at Castleview House, the block of flats in Runcorn, Cheshire, where he lives.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: But to an estate agent called Britské Reality - which translates as British Real Estate - working with investors hundreds of miles away in the Czech Republic, the flat Phil rents through his benefits was an exciting business opportunity.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: The estate agent's marketing material said the flat was a government-funded source of income for investors, where tenants were taken care of and the property was in excellent condition.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: A Czech investor bought it last year for £163,150, more than double the £75,000 cost of similar apartments in the block.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: The BBC has found more than 40 companies marketing similar properties to individuals in the UK and abroad, as businesses seek to profit from a government system intended to provide housing and support for vulnerable people.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: About a dozen of these companies work with a property developer called Lee Jones, whose company sold Phil's flat.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: The homes they are selling to investors are advertised as supported accommodation, a type of housing for people with issues including mental health problems or drug abuse issues, as well as people fleeing domestic violence.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: The BBC saw mould on ceilings and overflowing rubbish when we visited Castleview House Providers offering what is known as supported exempt accommodation are allowed to charge the taxpayer more than the usual housing benefit cap, because they have higher running costs.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: Tenants are entitled to care, support and supervision - although how much support should be provided is not defined.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: While there are legitimate providers helping people back into independent living, the BBC has previously reported on how some are exploiting the system by taking the higher housing benefit payments but failing to provide support .
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: Our latest investigation found companies marketing supported housing properties to people in Hong Kong, Macau, Nigeria, Turkey, the Netherlands, the UK and other countries as a "secure", "government-backed" investment.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: We also found adverts made misleading promises about the quality of the accommodation and support, with tenants saying they were receiving little or no care, while we observed examples of poor quality, unsafe accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: Housing charities and experts have told the BBC the sector has been transformed into a profit-generating machine at the expense of some tenants' safety, care, and dignity.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: Labour MP Abena Oppong-Asare, who chairs the Housing Select Committee, said it was "outrageous" that supported housing properties were being marketed as investments "particularly where there's public funds involved".
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: The BBC's findings were "alarming" and showed a sector "open to abuse", she added.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: Promotional materials such as this social media post advertise the homes as "Secure, Government-Backed Wealth" Lee Jones's company The Investment Room converted Castleview House in 2019 from an office block into more than 200 residential flats, including the one where Phil now lives.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: Then Jones partnered with Nurture Housing Association.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: His company granted Nurture a 25-year-lease on some of the flats, to provide housing for people on government benefits.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: Jones has a close business relationship with Nurture's chief executive Chris Smith, with the pair also acting as joint directors of other housing companies.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: Jones then worked with estate agents, which marketed the housing to investors in the UK and overseas using the regular cashflow generated by the 25-year lease with Nurture and the promise of government funding to justify inflated prices.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: Lee Jones and Nurture have repeated this with property developments across England, including in Doncaster, Rotherham, Stockton-on-Tees and Bradford.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: These type of properties are also in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland but are funded and regulated differently.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: Because neither profit-making private companies nor individuals can act as supported housing providers themselves, co-operation between developers, investors and publicly funded providers has become common.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: The Czech marketing material found by the BBC said Nurture provides housing for people with mental health issues who receive the "aftercare program pursuant to Section 117 of the Mental Health Act", meaning they have been sectioned and discharged from hospital with a detailed care plan.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: But Phil says he has never been sectioned under the Mental Health Act.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: He does have severe depression and anxiety, and he is currently out of work.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: But he says he has never had any support or care, or met anyone working for Nurture during his time at the flat.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: "Whoever marketed this property, the way they've worded it is total dishonesty," says Phil.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: But there were clues: bills addressed to someone called Jan Hála had been coming through the letterbox for months.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: Lee Jones told us that the properties his companies provide are "good quality accommodation" and he has no responsibility for the communal areas of Castleview House since he sold the freehold in 2021.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: He denied his relationship with Chris Smith amounted to a conflict of interest, but did not respond to questions about his role in marketing the properties.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: Jan Hála, the Czech investor who now owns Phil's flat, and the Britské Reality estate agency did not respond to requests for comment.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: We spoke to several other people living in flats run by Nurture Housing Association in Castleview House who said they were in supported accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: They reported receiving little or no help from Nurture but were afraid to speak out publicly for fear of eviction and becoming homeless.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: There is also evidence that marketing materials for investors buying flats in Castleview were misleading.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: Investors were told Nurture was providing "specialist supported housing" - a claim which is repeated on its website.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: But Nurture had not been registered as a specialised supported housing provider, the regulator said, and its claim to be providing this was "shocking".
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: In a statement, Nurture acknowledged that Castleview House is managed under a "general housing management model" and does not form part of its supported housing portfolio.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: It said it provided supported housing elsewhere through partners which were registered providers.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: It said the Czech advert found by the BBC related to "historic marketing material" produced by third parties.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: However, the BBC has seen marketing material from several other agents selling flats in Castleview House to investors, which also claim that Nurture is providing supported housing to the residents on a 25-year lease.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: Nurture said it is not directly involved with the companies marketing the properties.
sentences.article_title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad

sentences.text: Sir James was named as the Conservative Party candidate on Thursday Former home secretary and foreign secretary Sir James Cleverly has been selected as the Conservative candidate for mayor of London.

sentences.text: "The problems London faces are the symptoms.

sentences.text: The injunction granted by the High Court prevents Ryan Bridge and Raise the Colours from attaching flags and other items to public property Birmingham City Council has won a High Court injunction preventing unauthorised flags being attached to lamp-posts and other highway infrastructure across the city.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: The authority sought the order after thousands of St George's flags and union jacks were put up by supporters of anti-migrant group Raise the Colours from summer 2025 onwards.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: Council lawyers argued the displays created safety risks and fuelled tensions, while campaigners said the move would restrict freedom of expression.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: Judge Emma Kelly said there was a "compelling need" to grant the interim injunction.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: In her ruling, the judge said it would last until trial or further order of the court.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: The order applies to Raise the Colours' leader Ryan Bridge; Ben Cullen, who is also associated with the group; and persons unknown from attaching flags to street furniture and highway infrastructure.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: It also grants a power of arrest against Bridge and persons unknown, meaning police could arrest someone without a warrant if they are suspected of breaching the injunction.
sentences.article_title: Council wins legal fight against flags on lamp-posts

sentences.text: The council said anyone who breaches the order could be jailed for up to two years, fined or have their assets seized for contempt of court.

sentences.article_title: Home secretary plans to tackle 'corrosive' perception of two-tier policing

sentences.text: Sales of a baby sleeping bag have been halted in the UK by fashion retail chain Next, after a new mum raised the alarm over its safety.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: Emma Hunter, 29 from Norwich, contacted BBC Your Voice to say she realised the neck hole was far too big - meaning her daughter Rosie could potentially wriggle down, burying her face and risking suffocation.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: Emma recalls: "I woke up my husband and we both agreed there was no way we could put Rosie in it." Next says its own-brand, 2.5 tog pink floral sleep bag with removable sleeves that comes in three sizes, has been removed from the website and stores and a product recall is under way.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: Next will contact and advise customers who purchased the item from them.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: The sleeping bag is now unavailable on Next's website after safety fears were raised A spokesperson for Next said: "We can confirm the item has been removed from our website and all stores.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: A product recall is in place, and we are contacting all customers who purchased the item directly to advise them of the appropriate next steps." Emma says she started doing her own research that same night she realised the sleeping bag was unsuitable for Rosie.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: Although the product had a label stating that it met British standards, Emma discovered that the maximum neck circumference for that size of bag should be 32cm.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: When she measured the bag, the neck hole was 36cm.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: According to the British Retail Consortium (BRC), a significant hazard arises if a child slips through the neck opening of a sleep bag and the material covers the child's nose and mouth.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: They state that "suffocation can occur and may lead to the brain becoming starved of oxygen, which may result in asphyxia and potential brain damage or fatality." To limit this hazard, the EN 16781 standard specifies a maximum and minimum size for the neck opening circumference in relation to the child's height.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: For example, a sleep bag designed for a child 50 cm to 65 cm tall should have a minimum neck circumference of 28 cm and a maximum of 32 cm.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: Rosie, who is now three and a half months old, measured 59cm at the time the bag was bought.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: After flagging these issues to the company, Emma says she was surprised by their initial reaction.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: "They seemed quite laissez faire about it and just offered me a refund, but I said 'it's dangerous, surely you shouldn't be selling it any more and there should be a product recall?'" Emma was told by Next that they were looking into it and that their product team was examining the bag and would feed back.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: Emma's older brother died of Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS) as a baby so the risk to babies from suffocation is something close to her heart.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: She told the BBC: "I am more aware of this because of what happened to my brother and my family, but it shouldn't take an infant mortality to see change.
sentences.article_title: Sales of baby sleeping bag halted by Next after new mum raises alarm

sentences.text: "They didn't have any sense of urgency about it at all and I expected a big high street store like that to have a certain standard.

sentences.text: You put your trust into these retailers.

sentences.text: CT scans before (left) and after treatment with daraxonrasib plus chemotherapy (gemcitabine and nabpaclitaxel) showing multiple tumours that are no longer visible.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Yellow arrows indicate the tumours visible before treatment Experts are calling it the biggest breakthrough in pancreatic cancer treatment for decades - a daily pill that appears to shrink and possibly even eliminate tumours in some patients with one of the deadliest and hardest-to-treat cancers.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Cancer became undetectable on scans in one in 12 of the patients given daraxonrasib along with chemotherapy in early medical trials.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Tumours stopped growing in almost all of the 61 participants who had recently been diagnosed with advanced pancreatic cancer that had spread to other parts of the body.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: But doctors stress it is unclear how long it might keep the disease at bay and should not be seen as a cure.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Cancer Research UK called it "the biggest leap forward in decades" for pancreatic cancer patients.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: The charity's Dr Sam Godfrey told BBC News that the results were incredibly exciting.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: "What this new drug has done is it's found a way of drugging the undruggable.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: "We are finally seeing progress in pancreatic cancer which is so long overdue." Pancreatic cancer is notoriously hard to treat and has the lowest survival rate of all common cancers in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Although chemotherapy can shrink tumours a bit, the cancer often grows again.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Most patients with advanced disease survive months, not years.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Doctors hope the new treatment might offer patients more time, even if it cannot stop cancers for good.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: The trial followed patients for a year and a half, on average, and some did not see their cancer return during this time.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: "We are beginning to see not only a higher percentage of tumour response rates, but also deeper responses and a near doubling in the duration of disease control, which may eventually translate into longer survival," he said.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Daraxonrasib is a targeted inhibitor treatment that has already been approved in the US .
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: It works by locking on to and shutting off certain mutations, called RAS , external , found in most pancreatic cancers that drive tumour growth.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Dozens of other cancers, including lung and ovarian, can have similar mutations, meaning the drug might help lots of other patients too.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Dr Godfrey said: "I would hope that the early success that we are beginning to see in pancreatic cancer can also be rolled out to other cancers." He said longer trials and results were vital.
sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.article_title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish

sentences.text: Early efforts to contain coronavirus "were doomed to fail" because the test, trace and isolate system in the UK could only handle a relatively small number of cases, the seventh report of the Covid inquiry says in a damning assessment.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Across 245 pages the inquiry looks at everything from border controls to how well contact tracing worked.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Here's what you need to know.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The report said the virus was allowed to spread virtually unchecked in the first few months after community testing and contact tracing was abandoned in mid-March 2020, costing lives.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Ministers said this was because testing capacity was being overwhelmed.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: NHS Test and Trace was launched two months later and eventually became one of the biggest testing services in the world per head of population.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: In the end, more than £30bn was spent across the UK during the pandemic on testing, tracing and isolating.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Once established, it was effective.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: But in those early months the four UK nations were "effectively blind" to how quickly Covid was spreading, the inquiry said.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: It criticises the government for not having a robust test, trace and isolate system in place to start with, saying this, alongside other failures, meant harsher measures, including lockdown and school closures, were needed.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Inquiry chair Baroness Hallett said the UK should have been better prepared and learnt lessons from other countries that had experience of dealing with outbreaks of other infectious diseases, such as Sars.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Unlike the UK, places such as Hong Kong, South Korea, Singapore and Taiwan had established systems ready to go.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: This was despite the fact the UK had run a series of simulation exercises in the years leading up to Covid.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: They included Exercise Cygnus into a flu pandemic and Exercise Alice into Mers.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Both identified problems relating to test, trace or isolation, which appear not to have been fully acted on.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The report also raises the question of whether the government could have made use of non-government testing facilities in hospitals, universities and the private sector from the start, instead of just relying on 12 government labs.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: When people in the UK were told to isolate, "many felt forgotten and let down by the lack of practical or financial support when trying to follow the rules", says the report.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: In the early months of the pandemic, estimates suggested less than half of people were complying with the rules around isolating if infected.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Ministers and their advisers discussed this and fines of up to £10,000 were introduced for those who did not comply, which some experts have said was counter-productive.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Changes were made to allow people to claim statutory sick pay.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: But it was not until September in England – and later in Scotland and Wales – that £500 financial payments were introduced to help those on low incomes comply.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: More also needed to be done to provide practical support for things such as collecting medicines and shopping for food for those who did not have people to call on.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Suspending all flights from China to the UK in February 2020 could "have provided valuable additional time to prepare healthcare systems for the impact of the pandemic", said inquiry chair Baroness Hallett.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The report says the UK lacked a clear strategy for implementing border control measures early in the pandemic, which left the country in an "extremely vulnerable position".
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: By contrast, the UK government only requested travellers arriving from high-risk areas to self-isolate for 14 days.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The UK government implemented no further border control measures until June 2020.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The report says that border controls were a "critical gap in the UK's ability to limit the spread of the virus" and recommends that in the future "international border control measures should be in place at the earliest stages of a pandemic".
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The inquiry report is more positive about the use of smartphone apps, saying digital tools can have a "significant impact on reducing the spread of infection".
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: It quotes a mathematical modelling study from the US which estimates that, when 75% of people used a contact tracing app in the pandemic, infections were reduced by at least 50%.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: Three different apps were developed during Covid - one for England and Wales, another for Scotland and a third for Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: The inquiry says that took up "valuable time", and it recommends developing a UK-wide digital tool to use in any future outbreak.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: It says it is "fundamentally important" that apps and digital tools are as accurate as possible – and people have confidence in them.
sentences.article_title: Covid inquiry report: key findings on testing, tracing and 'the pingdemic'

sentences.text: In the summer of 2021, as Covid restrictions were relaxed, around 7% of all UK adults were told to self-isolate over a seven-day period, something dubbed by the press as the "pingdemic".

sentences.text: More than 200 doctors have had their details sent in error to the Times newspaper The doctors' regulator the General Medical Council (GMC) has apologised after it mistakenly sent information about more than 220 doctors to a national newspaper.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The information included summaries of complaints alleging antisemitism or Islamophobia against the doctors.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: For some of the medics involved, it was only when the GMC alerted them to the data breach that they discovered a complaint had been made about them.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The GMC says it is "very sorry" for the incident and has reported itself to the Information Commissioner's Office.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The GMC - an independent body that regulates doctors, physician associates and anaesthesia associates to protect patient safety - sent the information about 223 doctors to a journalist at the Times newspaper.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: While no names were revealed, GMC identification numbers were included, which would easily allow doctors to be found on the regulator's register.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: Some doctors have also raised concerns that their ethnicity was included in the data breach.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: All the medics involved have been the subject of a complaint involving either antisemitism or Islamophobia, dating from the Hamas attack on Israel in October 2023 to September 2026.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The GMC says it has a legal and statutory responsibility to investigate such claims.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: Meanwhile, the Times is understood to have promised not to make any of the  details public, but has said it will not delete the information.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: A spokesman for the doctor's trade union, the British Medical Association (BMA), condemned the release of personal information.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: "The BMA is aware that a number of doctors have received communication from the GMC to say that it erroneously sent personal identifiable data about them to the Times newspaper when responding to a media request," it said.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: "The GMC must take action to ensure such a breach never occurs again." The BMA said it would look at ways to support members affected and urged them to make contact via their website.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: A doctors' campaign group, The Doctors' Association UK (DAUK), called for an independent investigation into the error.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: "If a doctor sent identifiable patient information to a newspaper, they could expect to be referred to the GMC," said Dr Matt Kneale, DAUK co-chairman.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: "The GMC should hold itself to the same standard of confidentiality it expects from doctors.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: Just over a quarter of complaints over Islamophobia - 26% - have led to disciplinary action.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: But other complaints were closed, having failed to reach the threshold for investigation.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: The GMC said it had contacted the doctors affected to explain what had happened, to apologise and provide information and support.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: A spokesperson added: "We recognise the concern this will cause to both those impacted personally and other registrants and we are very sorry this happened.
sentences.article_title: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper

sentences.text: "Our priority continues to be supporting those affected and taking steps to reduce the impact of this incident." Clarification 20 November: This article was amended on 19 November to remove references to the information being 'leaked'.

sentences.text: Adverts for tests and services relating to low testosterone are allowed but must be rooted in evidence, the regulator said Five adverts by online healthcare provider Voy have been banned by the watchdog for making misleading claims linked to low testosterone in men.

sentences.article_title: Voy at-home test kit adverts banned over low testosterone claims

sentences.text: From Spring 2027, under 16s will no longer be able to access several social media applications More than 300,000 young people in Britain will work with researchers to help understand how the UK's forthcoming social media ban for under-16s could affect mental health.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: The studies will examine the habits of the children and teenagers, including whether they spend less time on their phones and what they are replacing scrolling with.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Ten different projects have been commissioned, taking place across England, Wales and Scotland, to help reflect a diverse range of teenagers.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: The social media ban, beginning in spring 2027, will follow a similar model to that already introduced in Australia to stop children accessing platforms such as Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Apps such as Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, Snapchat and YouTube will be banned under new rules The work, funded by health charity The Wellcome Trust, will help inform future online safety policies in the UK and internationally, with some early results available before the ban happens.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Researchers will use wearable technology, smartphones, digital diaries and surveys to collect data to see how young people respond to the ban, both physically and mentally.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: And they will check whether young people find ways to circumvent restrictions.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Dr Camilla Iannone, research lead at Wellcome, said it was a once-in-a-generation opportunity to study at scale how social media and its restrictions affected youth mental health.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: "We really don't think that this is a simple binary question of whether social media is good or bad, or whether restrictions work or don't work.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: "Instead, the teams will study whether changing young people's digital environment leads to meaningful changes in their mental health and wellbeing." Participants are being recruited to reflect a diverse range of young people, including different genders and sexual orientations.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: People with existing mental health conditions, such as anxiety and depression, will also be included, as well as young people who are neurodivergent.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Groups have been set up at Cardiff University, the University of Oxford, the University of Birmingham, King's College London, the University of Edinburgh, the University of Manchester, the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, and University College London.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: Online forum Reddit and a digital rights group are currently involved in a high court battle in the country, arguing that the law change is unconstitutional.
sentences.article_title: Largest British study to check social media ban's effect on youth mental health

sentences.text: There have also been reports of Australian teens finding ways to get round the ban - with the UK government promising to make sure tougher blocks are in place.

sentences.text: This video can not be played 'When I found out about Breast Friends it was the best thing ever' Annette Farrington-Moore says a charity became a lifeline after her breast cancer diagnosis, and now the group that helped her is celebrating a major milestone with a royal seal of approval.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: Run by volunteers with lived experience of the disease, Breast Friends Solihull provides emotional and practical support with many involved forging lifelong friendships.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "You don't want to trouble family and they don't really understand what you're going through emotionally," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "The kids were there for me but when I found out about Breast Friends it was like the best thing ever." Those who run the group firmly believe that no-one should go through breast cancer alone.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: The organisation has supported thousands of people affected by breast cancer over the last 25 years, and has juar been awarded the King's Award for Voluntary Service.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: Annette Farrington-Moore was diagnosed with breast cancer in January 2025 Annette, 64, was diagnosed with breast cancer last year.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: Widowed and feeling low, she found solace in attending meetings and events put on by the group.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "Whenever you're ill and you haven't got your husband, there's no one there to look after you like they would," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "So having Breast Friends, you know there's somebody on the end of the phone who can be there for you." The charity provides services such as gardening and cleaning to allow people to rest during treatment, as well as support with bras, wigs and hospital visits.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: It has also raised money to fund hospital equipment.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: The charity's committee members say they believe in prescribing a healthy dose of laughter and friendship Chris Pile was diagnosed with breast cancer 20 years ago, when she was a nurse and mother of two young children.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: She is now vice-chair of the group and helps lift others when they're down.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "I joined Breast Friends when I finished my chemotherapy and radiotherapy, and I found it really uplifting," she explained.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: Everybody was so positive and friendly, and I got involved straight away because that's the kind of person I am.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "I've organised days and nights out, summer suppers and the Christmas dos." Now vice-chair of the group, Chris Pile was diagnosed with breast cancer 20 years ago Chair Deborah Douglas has had breast cancer twice, first in 2003 and again earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: She said she has now been given "the all clear" following treatment.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: Her experiences mean she knows first-hand what support to offer, explaining that a diagnosis can be "scary and frightening".
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: Chair of Breast Friends Deborah Douglas said achieving the Kings Award for Voluntary Service meant more people would hear about the group and ask for help Her first diagnosis led her to seek help from Breast Friends.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: "I walked in and I saw women who weren't sad.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: They were all happy and so uplifting, and they basically supported me from the moment I walked in.
sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.article_title: 'It's a lifeline': Breast cancer support group that's helped thousands

sentences.text: Alan Milburn has said the country needs a "complete system reset" to bring down the number of young people not in work or education - known as "Neets".
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: In a major review, published on Tuesday, , external he suggested a raft of proposals to address the problem, which mostly cover England but he says can be adapted in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland too.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Each of his recommendations will need to be accepted by the government and implemented and paid for before they become reality - and that could take some time.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: So how might today's proposals affect you if you are Neet?
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Major report proposes welfare changes, apprenticeships and tax cuts to help 440,000 young people into work At the heart of the recommendations, Milburn says, is a new Youth Opportunity Service.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: He wants this to be implemented locally, with each area drawing up a plan to help their own young people.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: It would bring together employment, careers, health and practical support, with each young person getting a named adviser and a personalised plan.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn wants areas to begin building their Youth Opportunity Service from 2027, with one in place everywhere by the end of 2029.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Within 14 days of entering the service, a young person would then meet with a named adviser.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Within four weeks, they would have their "personalised participation plan", setting out what both the support services and the young person involved would do, and when.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Jobs wise, Milburn wants there to be initiatives like work placements of up to 12 weeks, structured volunteering opportunities, and help to create businesses.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: He also wants those who remain Neet - despite enagaging with support - to be provided with a paid six-month job, funded by the government.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: The government has already committed to a legal guarantee of job support in theory , but the exact workings still need to be worked out.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Alongside more work opportunities, Milburn wants a "major expansion" in further education for 18- to 24 year-olds, as well as more apprenticeship places.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Over the next decade, he wants the number of young people completing an apprenticeship to double, and for apprenticeships to rival university as an option for school leavers.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Colleges should also get new funding for participation and work-readiness, the review says, initially targeted at 16- and 17-year-olds who are Neet or at serious risk of becoming so.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: He also wants the government to develop new industry-led technical colleges and specialist campuses.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: If the reforms are enacted, Milburn says young people should have better access to high-quality further education and apprenticeships by 2028.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Under the proposals, schools, colleges and universities would be judged by whether pupils make successful transitions into further learning and work, rather than just academic achievements.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: By 2036, he wants 35% of each year group to have started a high-quality apprenticeship by age 25.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: The young people caught up in Britain's Neets crisis At a glance: Key proposals from Milburn's Neets report Milburn has said he wants a fundamental transformation of how mental health support for young people is delivered.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Young people who are Neet should be guaranteed fast-track access to services within three months, according to his recommendations.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: This would include things like vocational rehabilitation, talking therapies and counselling as part of a young person's plan with their local Youth Opportunity Service - which would be rolled out between 2027 and 2029 under the plans.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: There has been a big rise in mental distress among children and young people in recent years, and Milburn's report comes at a time the NHS is facing huge pressures.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn wants mental health support to be available for all young people digitally, without needing a diagnosis.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Some areas are already using these approaches, but scaling them up would be a major challenge and would take a long time to introduce across the board.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Plus, Milburn wants "fitness to work" notes to be taken out of the hands of GPs and put into community work and health teams, and for them to be "a trigger for help - not simply a certificate of absence".
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn wants these changes to begin in 2027 and would be linked to the Youth Opportunity Service rollout, which would be complete by 2029 under the plans.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn has said he wants companies to be incentivised to employ more young people, with the report highlighting a competitive jobs market and applicants who often fail to hear back from potential employers.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: The report includes three asks of employers: to create more genuine first jobs, more first-job apprenticeships and much wider access to meaningful work experience.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Plus, Milburn wants large employers to find ways of responding to rejected job applicants.

sentences.text: Too many university students can use AI to complete assessments without staff finding out, the higher education regulator in England has said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The Office for Students (OfS) said "a significant proportion" of assessments are unsupervised and many can be completed to a high standard with AI, sometimes in minutes.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It said this posed a "significant risk" to their credibility, and closed-book and practical exams were the most effective forms of assessments.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities UK said many institutions had "made substantial changes" to make assessments "AI-proof".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities that do not meet OfS quality standards could soon be banned from charging increased tuition fees or have caps imposed on their student numbers, under proposals that are now being consulted on.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The new research from the OfS and Advance HE, a charity that gives awards for teaching excellence, is based on the views of 244 higher education staff and 91 students from at least 127 universities.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It said "a significant proportion of assessments" were in "unsupervised, non-controlled formats where AI can be accessed by students completing them".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "Many of these can be completed to a high standard using AI tools with limited engagement from students," it added.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It also concluded it was "frequently possible" for students to use AI "in ways that cannot be reliably detected".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Unsupervised assessment can include coursework, but also remote online exams.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: They were rolled out widely during Covid, and research from Swansea University , external last year suggests 93 universities in the UK still use them in some form.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Josh Fleming, director of strategy and delivery at the OfS, said there were "fantastic" examples of universities seizing opportunities presented by AI, but there should be "far greater use of AI-free assessment".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "It also presents a generational risk to the system as it stands, threatening to undermine students' learning and institutions' ability to assess them," he said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Kathryn Harrison-Graves, deputy chief executive at Advance HE, said students wanted "greater clarity about what is expected of them" but staff had "varying levels of confidence and support".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Some staff, meanwhile, were receiving lots of assignments that looked the same, and did not think their institution's assessments were "fit for purpose".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Other staff described a "polarised atmosphere" between students who used AI and other "conscientious objectors" who avoided it on environmental and other grounds.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The research said AI literacy for students was important during and after university, and some institutions were clearly communicating to students where AI can and cannot be used in assessments.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: But it said there was "an urgent need" to ensure that remote or "non-secure" assessments "maintain their validity despite the availability of AI tools, meaning they effectively assess the knowledge and skills they are designed to measure".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "If it becomes possible to complete an assessment using AI without the knowledge and skills being tested, the assessment should be replaced," it added.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities UK, which represents more than 140 institutions, said universities were "making significant progress" adapting to AI.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "There is further to go but many have made substantial changes to how they assess students.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: This includes more in-person exams, presentations, vivas, process-based assessment and assessments that integrate AI in a controlled way," a spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "It's time to get rid of the outdated methods, that have been kept around in the name of tradition, and instead encourage the innovative practice we see across the sector, co-designed with students based on what they want from higher education," he said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Sweeping reforms are needed to help 440,000 more young people into work, according to former minister Alan Milburn.

sentences.text: Almost one million young people aged 16 to 24 in the UK are not in education, employment or training - or "Neet" - a current rate of 13%, which Milburn wants to fall to around 5% within a decade.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: But Helen Whately, Conservative shadow work and pensions secretary, said Milburn's proposals were in parts "too cautious" and too reliant on the "expensive hand of the state".

sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: "We've got to get on with it, it's going to take time but I want to make sure every young person has a chance to earn or learn," he told BBC Breakfast on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: The review says that, in 2024/25, for every £1 spent helping young people into work or education, £25 was spent on youth benefits.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: By 2036, it says the aim should be for that ratio to be £2 on benefits for every £1 on work support.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: "If we can get the benefits bill down, that is a good thing, but this is not about saving costs, it's about improving young people's lives," Milburn said.

sentences.text: The service would put a young person in touch with a named adviser to help to secure them an apprenticeship, college place, supported employment or a job within four months.

sentences.text: The review's key welfare measures, some of which have already been announced , suggest replacing these benefits for under-25s with a new Youth Allowance at the current base rate of Universal Credit for young people, and a new Additional Cost Allowance to replace Pip.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: She has fluctuating physical and mental health problems, including occasional seizures caused by functional neurological disorder, which recently left her needing crutches.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: Milburn, a Labour MP from 1992 to 2010, says many young people are desperate for opportunity, but that many get knocked back repeatedly.
sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.article_title: 'Complete system reset' needed to get 440,000 young people into work, says major review

sentences.text: Although they help him with applications to prospective employers, Josh says "none of them are getting back, and if they do they say you've not got the spot".

sentences.text: "Reform UK would act now to axe Labour's jobs tax, double the number of apprenticeships and end university scam courses that laden students with debt," she said.

sentences.text: Education Secretary Lucy Powell says the government will "update and strengthen" Holocaust education within schools after a major review highlighted the "shocking scale" of antisemitism in British society.

sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The government has accepted all of the 27 recommendations made in the government-commissioned review including dedicated training for teachers and more consistent recording of incidents.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review
