sentences.text: Powell told the BBC it marked a "generational moment" to re-educate young people, among whom she said the issue of antisemitism was "particularly prevalent".
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: She said: "It's definitely a crisis and I think it's actually got worse since Sir David began this review.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: This has become a real challenge for Jewish people in our country, but also Jewish students and Jewish teachers working in our schools and colleges.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: "I do really feel it is a generational moment to educate this generation and the next – that is the job of education – to understand what antisemitism is in the modern world." Speaking on Holocaust education, the education secretary said new lessons will "challenge" some of the concepts that young people have.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The review also calls for stronger guidance on political impartiality for teachers.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Powell told the House of Commons "teachers should not bring their own political views into the classroom" but they should not avoid discussing important topics.

sentences.text: The review was launched following a series of high-profile incidents including the attack at Heaton Park synagogue in Manchester in October 2025, in which two men were killed.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Separate reviews were also commissioned into antisemitism in healthcare and into public order and hate crime laws.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The BBC revealed in August that the Bell review had found Jewish schoolchildren were experiencing regular harassment and abuse.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: It also found that headteachers of some Jewish schools were spending more of their time dealing with security arrangements than educational matters .
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The review also recommends that the government sets up a type of hotline where school leaders can access immediate advice on tackling antisemitism.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Bell, who is now vice-chancellor of the University of Sunderland, heard evidence from pupils, teachers, governors and parents across state and independent schools, as well as from community organisations.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: He told the BBC: "This is not just a report for Jewish children in Jewish schools.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: This is for all children and young people in all schools and colleges.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: We know that antisemitism crosses all boundaries." Earlier this month, the BBC was given rare access inside a Jewish school in Hertfordshire, where pupils and staff operate under tight security, amid heightened concerns about antisemitism.

sentences.text: Spencer Lewis, the executive headteacher of Yavneh College, said that security was an "innate part" of his role.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: "When you come in in the morning, there are high gates, high fences, lots of security cameras.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: We have four full-time security staff.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: And it sort of just becomes part of what you do," he said.

sentences.text: "We think about it a lot." In response to the recommendations, the government will also encourage schools to adopt the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA)'s working definition of antisemitism, although it cannot make it compulsory.

sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: However, some of the IHRA definition's examples of antisemitic behaviour have proven controversial.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: "Antisemitism in our schools is real, it is widespread, and too often it goes unrecognised and unchallenged." "One-off assemblies are not enough, and neither is sitting pupils in front of a video.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Young people need the space to ask difficult questions, challenge their own assumptions and understand that antisemitism did not start or end with the Holocaust." The National Education Union raised concerns about creating a "hierarchy of racism" and adopting the IHRA definition.

sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: One of the studies mentioned on the podcast comes from the University of Bristol , external , which found that around a quarter of children appear to understand some form of deception by the time they are 10 months old.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: Prof Elena Hoicka, who led the study, says it was fascinating to see how "surprisingly young" kids could be so adept and cunning, including her own.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: "As a mother of three, I can certainly vouch for how artful and wily they can be.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: "Hiding under the table or in the bathroom to eat sweets or chocolate is their common ploy." Hoicka says that the kind of deception a child uses from the age of two is quite basic - like pretending not to hear their parent or denying they've done something.

sentences.text: CBeebies Parenting Download Clinical psychologist Dr Jade Redfern explains why young children may lie and Traitors winner Rachel Duffy discusses how she encourages hers to tell the truth "It could also extend to doing forbidden activities in secret," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: She says they also start to withhold information.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: For instance, truthfully telling their parents that their sibling has hit them but omitting the fact that they hit their sibling first.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: These deceptions are a sign of them developing something Redfern calls "theory of mind".
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: Ada, age two, deceives her mum by hiding in the bathroom to eat chocolate she had stolen "As children grow up, we want them to learn and develop the skill that they are their own human being with a separate mind and intentions," she explains.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: "This is how [they] develop the skills in empathy, or being able to think about another person's thoughts and feelings that might differ from their own." Another reason a child might lie is self-preservation as they don't want to upset or disappoint their parent.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: "All human beings are driven by attachment," says Redfern.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: "[Children are] driven by being able to preserve that relationship with their caregivers as they depend upon it." Early on, they learn what brings them closer to their caregiver and what pulls them apart, she says.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: With this in mind, Redfern thinks you can encourage honesty by creating a safe environment for a child to tell the truth.
sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

sentences.text: "[We] have to think about ways we can help children feel safe enough to tell us the truth [when] they've made a mistake... and they don't want to disappoint us." This is something Rachel Duffy, who won the latest series of The Traitors, tells the CBeebies Parenting podcast that she has been trying to do.

sentences.article_title: Why fibbing about stolen snacks is an important part of childhood

Redfern says this is a good example of how to deal with such a situation and that there are occasions when a lie, or nuance, might be appropriate - such as when they receive a gift they don't want or describe other people physically.

sentences.text: This video can not be played Why is a spacecraft flying to Mercury?
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: After an eight-year journey travelling almost six billion miles (10bn km), a spacecraft called BepiColombo is about to reach its final destination and get into orbit around Mercury.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: It will be entering an extremely hostile environment: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun and temperatures can reach a fierce 430C and then plunge to -180C, and it is constantly blasted with intense solar radiation.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: Until now, the planet has been little explored but the hope is this mission will solve some of Mercury's major mysteries.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: These include uncovering why there is ice in its craters despite its proximity to the Sun, and understanding the mysterious hollows that are dotted all over its surface.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: "I think it's a little bit of an under-loved planet in the inner Solar System, but I think that's one of the reasons why it is so compelling," said Prof Emma Bunce, from Leicester University, who is a principal investigator on the mission.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: With the spacecraft heading deep into the inner Solar System, it has had to battle the Sun's immense gravitational pull.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: So it has had its brakes on for the entire journey, and has also taken a very convoluted path - looping once around the Earth, twice around Venus and six times around Mercury -  to slow it down enough to get into orbit.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: This journey should have taken seven years, but a problem with BepiColombo's propulsion system meant the already epic voyage was extended by a year.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: The final manoeuvre to get into orbit is a perilous one: it needs to perform a 37-minute handbrake turn to be grabbed by the planet's gravity.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: If anything goes wrong, the spacecraft could hurtle past Mercury.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: A close up view of the scarred surface of Mercury Only two spacecraft have visited Mercury until now - both Nasa missions.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: Mariner-10 flew past the planet three times in the 1970s, and then the Messenger spacecraft arrived at Mercury in 2011 and spent four years in orbit.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: But there is still much to discover about this tiny world.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: Mercury is only a bit bigger than our Moon, and is covered in ancient volcanoes, towering cliffs and colossal craters.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: And time on Mercury passes in a mind-bending way.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: The planet zips around the Sun so quickly, a year on Mercury lasts just 88 Earth days.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: But it turns incredibly slowly on its own axis, so a single day there lasts 59 Earth days.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: These strange hollows have not been seen anywhere else in the Universe As well as investigating why Mercury has ice in its craters in the polar regions, the mission will also spend time studying strange dents in the planet's surface.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: There are thousands of hollows all over it.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: They are shallow but with steep sides and often clustered together, and in planetary terms, they are young: about 100,000 years old.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: Scientists know they are not impact craters - larger pockmarks on the surface caused by colliding space rocks - but they are not really sure what the hollows are or how they formed.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: BepiColombo will also help to study another aspect of Mercury that has been puzzling researchers.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: Despite the planet's tiny size, it has a huge metal core.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: Prof Emma Bunce said that the planet could once have been much bigger, but was potentially the victim of a "hit and run" early in its history.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: "One of the explanations is that the mantle was stripped away in a large collision," she explained.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: "Or it's a combination of collisions over a longer period of time that then strips away its outer outer regions, its mantle and its crust, and leads to the planet that we see today." Or she said, it could have just formed that way in a metal-rich part of the early Solar System.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: A life-size model of BepiColombo is on display at the Science Museum in London Unusually, this is a sort of "buy one get one free" mission - there are two spacecraft onboard.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: A few weeks after arriving at Mercury they will separate.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: An ESA craft will study the surface close-up, the other, which belongs to JAXA, will view the planet from a distance.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: A life-size model of BepiColombo is on display at the Science Museum in London.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: It was used to test the craft while it was being put together.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: Jessica Marshall, a systems engineer at Airbus, who built the spacecraft, showed us Bepi's key features  - and said the moment of separation would be "nerve-wracking" for the team.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: The two spacecraft had to be very securely attached together for their launch and long journey, but now, eight years later, they have to delicately disconnect.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: "We have designed a special mechanism that we have thought very carefully about," said Marshall.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: Of course, they may uncover many more once they arrive.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: Africa is pushing for adaptation finance to be tripled by 2035, from an annual $40bn (£30bn) In Uganda's northern Karamoja region, Elijah Lobur and his family now eat just one meal a day.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: A severe drought that began in April has destroyed crops, while food brought in from elsewhere has become increasingly unaffordable.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "Seven months without rain has brought us to this point where we now live in hunger," the 44-year-old farmer, who lives with his grandmother, wife and five children, told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "Even some of the wild plants that we used to eat have withered and dried up." Local officials say more than 90% of crops have failed in the region, where agriculture is largely rain-fed.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: Further south, in Malawi, Mathews Nkhambala has experienced the devastating effects of flooding.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: In April 2024, barely a year after Tropical Cyclone Freddy devastated the country's southern region, floods displaced people in Chikwawa district.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: Nkhambala fled to higher ground with his wife and four children as floodwaters swept through his village.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "As we reached a safe height, we saw our house swept away right in front of our eyes.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: Everything I had was gone," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: He lost a harvest of 15 bags of sorghum and part of his farmland.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: His children were so traumatised that they stopped going to school.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "They refused to go to school for many months.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: They were so disturbed," he recalled.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: After relocating and trying to rebuild his life, Nkhambala is now facing another climate challenge - this time a lack of rain.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "This time we fear there may be no harvest.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: I have no clue what I will do." A government assessment after Cyclone Freddy found that Malawi had experienced more than 50 disasters linked to storms, floods, landslides and droughts since 1980, affecting millions of people.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: While Uganda and Malawi are suffering the effects of climate change and their governments are asking for assistance adapting to the new global weather patterns, they are among 23 African countries yet to submit National Adaptation Plans (NAPs) to the UN climate convention secretariat.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: These are the plans that detail how climate change has affected them and the risks they face, and so help make a case for what assistance they need.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: Without them, experts say, it becomes difficult to secure funding.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "Our region has experienced cyclical droughts for decades, but there has been no action plan to tackle these climate impacts," said Milton Lorpia, who works for Warrior Squad Foundation in Karamoja region of Uganda.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: The interpretation of that commitment remains contested.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: The proposal was not accepted for formal negotiations at the summit, although African negotiators have continued to push for it.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: The funding is intended to help vulnerable countries prepare for and withstand climate change-induced extreme weather, such as droughts, floods and wildfires.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: But the European Union, one of the largest providers of climate finance, says the priority should be ensuring existing commitments reach vulnerable countries rather than setting new funding targets.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "We haven't come to the table with additional monies or additional capital.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: It's about what we have committed already and ensuring it's deployed," Darragh O'Brien, who leads the EU delegation at COP31 on behalf of the Irish presidency of the Council of the EU, told a press conference.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: He acknowledged that developing countries faced difficulties accessing available funding, saying the process needed to be improved.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: Wopke Hoekstra, the European Commission's climate commissioner, also argued that the summit should focus on delivering existing pledges rather than making new ones.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: The scale of the need is substantial.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: According to the UN's Adaptation Gap Report published last year, sub-Saharan Africa requires about $51bn annually in adaptation finance, while the Middle East and North Africa needs $112bn.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: Globally, developing countries will need about $300bn annually by 2035, according to the UN's latest report.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: Yet they received only about 10% of that amount from developed countries in 2024.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: Climate-related loss and damage in Africa is projected to cost $440bn between 2020 and 2030, according to Nairobi-based think tank Power Shift Africa.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: Under the 2015 Paris climate agreement, developed countries are required to provide financial support to developing nations, including for climate adaptation.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: But why have so many African countries failed to prepare plans that could help them identify their needs and build resilience?
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "If you look closely, the countries that are yet to submit their NAPs are already dealing with multiple crises, including debt distress, economic pressures and other issues," said David Abudho, climate justice lead at the aid agency, Oxfam.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "Their governments' ability to invest in climate adaptation is limited." Sheila Apiny, regional climate justice adviser at ActionAid, said the lack of plans reflected a wider shortage of financial and technical support.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "The absence of NAPs in so many countries is, in itself, evidence of an adaptation finance and capacity gap," she argued.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: She said this created a vicious cycle - countries lack support to prepare their plans, while not having the plans makes it harder to secure funding for climate resilience.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "When countries lack adequate adaptation planning and, more importantly, the resources to implement those plans, governments are forced into a cycle of responding to disasters instead of preventing or reducing their impacts," said Amos Wemanya, senior climate adviser at Power Shift Africa.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "Instead of investing in early warning systems, climate-resilient agriculture, water security and flood protection, scarce public resources are repeatedly diverted towards emergency relief and reconstruction.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "Of course, having a comprehensive NAP helps countries prioritise investments and prepare proposals for climate finance," said Mahlet Eyassu Melkie, a senior strategic adviser to Ethiopia's COP32 presidency.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: Fred Njehu, a Pan-African political strategist at Greenpeace Africa, said their absence could nevertheless create significant obstacles.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "It is fair to acknowledge that missing adaptation plans act as a major functional barrier that severely bottlenecks the speed, volume and quality of international funding a country can access," he said.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: But having a plan does not guarantee the money needed to implement it.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "Even countries that have completed their NAPs have not received money anywhere near what they require for implementation of their adaptation plans," Apiny said.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: Kenya offers an example of how adaptation measures can help communities cope with climate pressures.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: But many vulnerable communities elsewhere on the continent are still waiting for similar interventions.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: Back in drought-hit Karamoja, Lobur wonders how different things might have been if farmers had access to small-scale irrigation schemes.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "We do have some underground water sources in some places.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: If there were proper plans and programmes, we could have tapped them to grow food, but we are having to live in hunger instead," Lobur said.

sentences.text: A bar-tailed godwit similar to Phil being fitted with a tracking device A bird named Phil has astonished conservationists by completing a 6,800-mile (10,900km) round trip from England's east coast to Siberia and back.
sentences.article_title: Wading bird called Phil tracked in epic migration to Siberia and back

sentences.text: Bar-tailed godwits are champion fliers, migrating between Britain and the Arctic, but the precise routes used by individual birds is largely unknown.
sentences.article_title: Wading bird called Phil tracked in epic migration to Siberia and back

sentences.text: Phil was fitted with a tiny solar-powered tracker that recorded his movements throughout the journey.
sentences.article_title: Wading bird called Phil tracked in epic migration to Siberia and back

sentences.text: The data showed he travelled from The Wash , external to the Wadden Sea, along the coasts of the Netherlands, Germany and Denmark, before continuing to Siberia.
sentences.article_title: Wading bird called Phil tracked in epic migration to Siberia and back

sentences.text: On his return, he crossed the Arctic Ocean to northern Norway, stopping on three islands before heading back through the Wadden Sea to The Wash.
sentences.article_title: Wading bird called Phil tracked in epic migration to Siberia and back

sentences.text: Bar-tailed godwits resting on the beach in the Wadden Sea Scientists say Phil's extraordinary travels highlight the importance of protecting the world's wetlands, which are havens for millions of migratory birds each year.
sentences.article_title: Wading bird called Phil tracked in epic migration to Siberia and back

sentences.text: Dr Nigel Clark, of the conservation charity, The Wash Wader Research Group, said The Wash is the UK's single most important coastal wetland for migratory waders, with spectacular numbers seen in autumn and winter.
sentences.article_title: Wading bird called Phil tracked in epic migration to Siberia and back

sentences.text: "Tracking birds like Phil the Godwit shows us how connected the Wash is with the rest of the flyway," he said.
sentences.article_title: Wading bird called Phil tracked in epic migration to Siberia and back

sentences.text: Jeff Kew, RSPB Coastal Advisor, said many migratory bird species cross borders, depending on a whole network of wetlands along the way.
sentences.article_title: Wading bird called Phil tracked in epic migration to Siberia and back

sentences.text: That's why it's so important to look after these special places." Bar-tailed godwits are wading birds of similar size to pigeons, but with long bills and legs.
sentences.article_title: Wading bird called Phil tracked in epic migration to Siberia and back

sentences.text: They are regarded as one of nature's long-distance endurance athletes, with one subspecies making the longest known non-stop migration of any bird, flying 8,425 miles (13,559km) from Alaska to New Zealand.

sentences.text: Pugh said the Strait of Hormuz has an "extraordinary natural world" beneath the surface A British endurance swimmer has completed a three-day swim through the Strait of Hormuz to draw attention to what he says is the environmental cost of the conflict involving Iran.
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: Lewis Pugh, who is a UN Patron of the Oceans, swam about 15km (9.3 miles) through the strategic waterway, a key route for oil shipments from the Middle East.
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: Pugh, 56, who was born in Plymouth, Devon said "war causes immense human suffering" but nature is "another casualty that receives far too little attention".
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: He is calling for an end to the fighting, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and action to address environmental damage caused by the conflict.
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: The Strait of Hormuz carries a significant share of global oil shipments from the Middle East The swimmer is believed to be the first person to attempt a long-distance swim in the Strait of Hormuz since the conflict began in March .
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: He swam from Musandam Island in the strait to the Cape of Hormuz, at the northern tip of Oman's Musandam Peninsula.
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: According to the Lewis Pugh Foundation, an oil tanker was struck by a projectile about 4km (2.5 miles) from where he was swimming on the first day.
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: On the second day, he saw flames rising above a headland separating him from the burning liquefied petroleum gas carrier Tara Gas and later passed close to the vessel while it was still on fire.
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: "My immediate thoughts were for the seafarers on board," Pugh said.
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: "The flames were enormous.
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: "War causes immense human suffering.
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: Lives are lost, families are torn apart, and homes, hospitals and schools can be destroyed in minutes," he said.
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: "But there is another casualty that receives far too little attention: nature itself.
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: And the damage can last long after the fighting has stopped." The Strait of Hormuz is one of the world's most important shipping routes and is also home to wildlife including dugongs, sea turtles and whale sharks.
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: Pugh said oil spills and other contamination could have long-term consequences for marine ecosystems including coral reefs, seagrass meadows and mangrove forests.
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: The project aims to create and restore habitats for amphibians and lizards Ponds are to be restored and freshwater habitats created for amphibians and reptiles at two former colliery sites in South Yorkshire.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife conservation cash targets ex-colliery sites

sentences.text: The Froglife charity has been awarded nearly £890,000 of Lottery cash to carry out the work in Rother Valley, as well as at sites in North and West Yorkshire.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife conservation cash targets ex-colliery sites

sentences.text: Kiveton and Dinnington Community Woodlands were originally regenerated through the National Coalfields Programme after the pits there closed in the 1990s.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife conservation cash targets ex-colliery sites

sentences.text: Sheila Grundry, from Froglife, said staff were "delighted" to work in the area because "freshwater will make a lasting difference for frogs and other wildlife and it's a great way for local people to learn new skills".
sentences.article_title: Wildlife conservation cash targets ex-colliery sites

sentences.text: The £889,761 investment in Froglife's Coalface to Wildspace project will also  help local communities connect with nature, according to the charity.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife conservation cash targets ex-colliery sites

sentences.text: Dinnington Woodland is one of the sites in Yorkshire which will be a focus of the project The aim of the project across Yorkshire is to create 48 new ponds, improve 93 existing freshwater habitats and establish new "neighbourhood wildlife corridors" like small ponds and bug hotels.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife conservation cash targets ex-colliery sites

sentences.text: These "corridors" will act as stepping stones for local wildlife from insects to birds, providing food, shelter and water to improve biodiversity across former industrial sites and help wildlife move between one habitat and another.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife conservation cash targets ex-colliery sites

sentences.text: Conservationist Andy Goff, project manager in Yorkshire, said the transformation of the sites would be for everyone.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife conservation cash targets ex-colliery sites

sentences.text: "We want people to engage with the nature that is on their doorstep and wildlife in general," he explained.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife conservation cash targets ex-colliery sites

sentences.text: "I'm really excited about getting people involved from all over Yorkshire." The Coalface to Wildspace project is funded by The National Lottery Heritage Fund for the next four years, with Froglife having already run similar projects in the Midlands and Scotland.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife conservation cash targets ex-colliery sites

sentences.text: Rother Valley MP Jake Richards said the project was important for the area.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife conservation cash targets ex-colliery sites

sentences.text: "These former industrial sites are an important part of our area's history," he said.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife conservation cash targets ex-colliery sites

sentences.text: "This project will help transform them into thriving habitats while creating opportunities for local people to get involved." Listen to highlights from South Yorkshire on BBC Sounds , catch up with the latest episode of Look North Wildlife habitat taking shape at former coal mine

sentences.text: Sean Cairncross (left) was appointed by the Trump administration The top cyber-security official in the US government is leaving his post after a little over a year in the job.

sentences.text: White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross was fired after losing the confidence of the White House chief of staff, Stephen Miller, according CBS, the BBC's US news partner.

sentences.text: Asked about his removal on Friday, President Donald Trump said it was because he was not "good enough".
sentences.article_title: White House removes cyber-security chief after series of tech outages

sentences.text: His firing comes after a string of tech outages which hit banking, air traffic control and other sectors.
sentences.article_title: White House removes cyber-security chief after series of tech outages

sentences.text: US officials said the outages were not caused by cyberattacks but the blackouts had sparked scrutiny from members of Congress who demanded a clearer explanation of what went wrong.
sentences.article_title: White House removes cyber-security chief after series of tech outages

sentences.text: There has been no official confirmation of the removal of Cairncross but Secretary of State Marco Rubio posted on X , external to say Department of Defense chief information officer Kirsten Davies was the new national cyber director.

sentences.text: The Dutch privacy watchdog, the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (AP), has told people not to buy smart glasses, saying they can get things dangerously wrong.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: It said in its tests of six glasses available on the Dutch market, the devices advised a user on how to date a child, misread medicine instructions, and claimed to have called an ambulance when they had not.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: While the AP is advising people not to buy the smart glasses, it stopped short of calling for them to be banned from sale.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: The authority is not revealing which glasses it tested, saying only that prices ranged from under €100 (£84) to over €500 and originated from different continents.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: The research follows growing concerns about privacy risks associated with smart glasses, in particular the misuse of the tech to film women without consent , or to record in places where filming is usually prohibited such as healthcare settings.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: Meta, a leading seller of the glasses, recently released a version without a camera with some commentators suggesting this was a response to the privacy backlash.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: It is unknown if the investigation included Meta's glasses.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: The AP told the BBC it would not name the products it tested.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: The BBC has approached Meta, TCL and HTC - all major manufacturers of smart glasses - for comment.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: Previously, these firms have been keen to highlight positive uses of smart glasses.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: Meta has highlighted the assistance they can provide to people with visual impairments.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: Its smart glasses use AI to describe things in the wearer's environment or to read text.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: The AP recognises the glasses can be valuable for people who need help to understand their surroundings.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: But for these users, it argues it is particularly important that AI is reliable.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: AP said in its testing of the unnamed brands, it found the advice given could be wrong.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: During a simulated emergency in which CPR resuscitation advice was requested, the AP found one pair of glasses claimed several times an ambulance was on the way - but emergency services had not been contacted.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: It said the AI also made child protection errors, with potentially serious consequences.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: One pair of glasses gave dating advice to an adult who indicated a romantic interest in a minor.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: The glasses also made errors when reading instructions inside medicine packages, as well as with interpreting severe weather warnings.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: And the AP was concerned smart glasses could be used to secretly film people, highlighting the ease with which lights, which warn that a device is recording, could be obscured.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: It said with some glasses these lights could be covered with tape and they would still work, despite some manufacturers claiming they would not function.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: Meanwhile, in some glasses, the AP found serious security flaws which meant someone nearby could connect without permission, view recordings, or even operate the camera remotely.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: It warned data recorded by the glasses was often exported outside the EU.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: In February, reports revealed outsourced workers were able to view sensitive content recorded on Meta smart glasses Meta said at the time such workers might sometimes review content, including video and images, in order to help improve its AI .
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: It said it took the protection of people's data very seriously, and was constantly refining its efforts and tools in that area, and would filter it first to blur faces in images.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: The AP investigation was not primarily focused on data protection - instead it was concerned with algorithms and AI.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: In the UK Paul Arnold, chief executive of privacy watchdog the Information Commission, who has a severe visual impairment has previously stressed the complexity of the argument , external around smart glasses.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: "They can help me and others better understand our surroundings, access information and navigate the world with greater confidence," he wrote in September.
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: But he said he had been "shocked and appalled by some of the irresponsible and harmful ways people are using these technologies".
sentences.article_title: Dutch watchdog tells people not to buy AI smart glasses

sentences.text: After years of anticipation and delays, as well as controversy around worker rights, Grand Theft Auto 6 has completed its phased worldwide release and is available to gamers everywhere, including the UK.

sentences.text: GTA 6 is set to become one of the world's most popular entertainment products ever, with fans booking time off work, and schools warning students not to bunk off.

sentences.text: Some schools have reminded parents and pupils to prioritise study over the game, which has an 18 rating , external for "strong graphic violence, strong sexual themes and use of illegal drugs".
sentences.article_title: UK joins in GTA 6 frenzy as game becomes available worldwide

sentences.text: One school in Essex incentivised pupils to attend with prizes such as vouchers, Christmas dinners and a pass to skip the lunch queue.

sentences.text: Helen Fraser's final television acting role was in an episode of Doctors in 2015 British television, theatre and film star Helen Fraser, who was perhaps best known for her role in the hit prison drama Bad Girls, has died.

sentences.text: The actress, who also appeared in episodes of Coronation Street and The Royle Family, reportedly died on 10 November at Yaxley House Care Home, in Eye, Suffolk.

sentences.text: Born in Oldham, Greater Manchester, she had lived in Wickham Skeith, in Suffolk, with her late husband Peter Handford.
sentences.article_title: Bad Girls star Helen Fraser dies aged 84

sentences.text: From 2004 until 2019, she was also an ambassador for East Anglia's Children's Hospices (EACH).
sentences.article_title: Bad Girls star Helen Fraser dies aged 84

sentences.text: The charity said it was "deeply saddened" by her death and would "remember her with enormous fondness and gratitude".

sentences.text: "Helen was very special to us and a wonderful ambassador, supporter and friend who worked tirelessly to champion our cause," a spokesperson said.

sentences.text: "Whether fundraising, attending events, opening our shops or rallying our volunteers, Helen brought incredible warmth, empathy and joy.
sentences.article_title: Bad Girls star Helen Fraser dies aged 84

sentences.text: "She had a wonderful way with people and made a lasting impression on all those fortunate enough to spend time in her company." The actress first trained at the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London before making her breakthrough in the 1963 film Billy Liar.

sentences.text: The Games Rating Authority, based in Stevenage, gets to play the games long before release The latest Grand Theft Auto game brings the franchise's trademark violence and adult storytelling to the latest generation of gaming hardware.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: But long before its release, examiners at the Games Rating Authority , external (GRA), based in Stevenage, Hertfordshire, got to play the game to decide its appropriate age rating.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: They analysed its content before assigning a PEGI age rating , external of 18, which covers 38 European territories.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: But who decides a game is for adults only, and how do they make that decision?
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: The Games Rating Authority administers PEGI age ratings on physical games in Europe Video games experience a similar process to films shown in UK cinemas, where examiners from the British Board of Film Classification watch each film before deciding its rating.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: But rating games presents a unique challenge.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: Modern games can contain huge worlds that take months to explore.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: Some allow players to make their own choices, meaning two people can have vastly different experiences.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: Developers first complete a GRA questionnaire disclosing any contentious content and provide at least two hours of footage, along with transcripts of the game's dialogue.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: Examiners study this material, logging timestamps for instances of blood, gore, horror, drug use or bad language.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: Examiner Sadie West is a fan of role-playing video games Lifelong gamer Sadie West joined the GRA believing it would be the dream job: being paid to play games.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: She says: "I definitely look at it more analytically when I'm playing here.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: "Since I've started here, I play games a lot less at home, but because I play in such a different way at work to what I'm playing at home, I can still enjoy it." West uses her skills with a controller to explore choices and scenarios that developers may not have captured on video.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: She says: "Things like, is there an NPC (non-playable character) that I can go up to, and can I attack them?
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: Or what happens if my character jumps off a bridge?
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: "Sometimes I die on purpose to see what a character death would look like." Many games, like Grand Theft Auto VI, feature large sprawling worlds for players to explore When playing games in her own time West hates hurting NPCs, but admits at work: "Unfortunately I have to be a bit evil sometimes".
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: She will typically play a game for several days, checking for blood, suggestive costumes and potentially exploitative in-game purchases.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: She says: "Once I'm happy that I've seen everything that would impact the rating, I then go through and I write up a report." That report is kept on record, while a version without plot spoilers is shared online for parents and players to read.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: Examiners follow strict classification criteria overseen by a panel that includes child welfare experts and psychologists.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: Ian Rice, director general of the GRA, says the criteria ensure ratings are applied "consistently and fairly".
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: Violence is only one element that is analysed, but shows how context can affect the classification: PEGI 3 & 7: Child-friendly, cartoon-like violence, such as in Minecraft, Rocket League, Roblox or Mario.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: PEGI 12: Unrealistic violence between humans, this could be games like Fortnite which have no blood or injury detail.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: PEGI 16: Realistic violence between humans, can include visible blood and pain reactions.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: PEGI 18: These games include what is classified as "gross violence", with high levels of blood and gore, or violence directed at innocent civilians.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: Sexually graphic content and the glamorisation of illegal drug use also trigger an automatic 18 rating.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: Some might wonder why games need adult content at all.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: Rice points out games can cover mature themes just like other forms of storytelling.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: He says: "Just because it's in a game doesn't mean somebody's making light of it.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: Rice says the authority maintains a dialogue with developers and offers advice throughout the development process.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: Rice himself is a keen gamer, but as a parent he is keen to stress the importance of the age rating system.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: Rice adds: "Every child is different, and parents know their children best.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: He has been in big-budget blockbusters like Twilight, Tenet and The Batman, as well as a string of quirky arthouse films - so what clues can Robert Pattinson's past roles give us about what he might be like as James Bond?

sentences.text: Every actor creates a new James Bond, and Pattinson is one of the best in the business at crafting a memorable character.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: He can be granite-faced or goofy, and everything in between.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: He cites Pattinson's performance as a brooding heartthrob in teen vampire franchise Twilight, his suave and quick-witted secret agent in Christopher Nolan's Tenet, the withdrawn and focused title character in The Batman, and the ruthless and manipulative Antinous in Nolan's The Odyssey.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: "Wouldn't it be interesting to see Bond go a little bit darker?" she suggested to the BBC's World Service.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: "But also what he's got, and I'd like him to do more of, is comedy.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: And goodness knows, we need a Bond who can handle humour." Unusually for a James Bond actor, one word that has cropped up frequently is "weird".
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: Earlier this month, Pattinson was described as "the weirdest guy in Hollywood" by the Celebrating Cinema podcast , external .
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: "Pattinson is an actor who makes bold, interesting, risky choices.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: For such a handsome guy, he can bring the weird, and then some," wrote Chris Hewitt in Empire , external .
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: "About 0.07 seconds after the announcement, people were already anticipating the weird with his Bond.

sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: The bill has been proposed by Nigeria's president Nigerian President Bola Tinubu has asked parliament to decriminalise attempted suicide, proposing medical support instead of prosecution for those who survive.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide

sentences.text: The proposal seeks to shift Nigeria's approach from criminal punishment to treatment and rehabilitation.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide

sentences.text: It follows years of calls for reform from mental health professionals.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide

sentences.text: A separate bill seeking to decriminalise attempted suicide has already passed its second reading in the Senate.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide

sentences.text: Under Nigeria's law, attempted suicide is a criminal offence with those convicted facing up to one year's imprisonment, a fine or both.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide

sentences.text: The Senate bill also seeks to replace criminal penalties for attempted suicide with medical treatment, rehabilitation and support.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide

sentences.text: It was sponsored by Senator Asuquo Ekpenyong, who has argued that prosecuting people who survive suicide attempts could discourage those experiencing suicidal thoughts from seeking help.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide

sentences.text: He also warned that families might conceal such incidents for fear of prosecution and social stigma.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide

sentences.text: He stressed that the bill is not aimed at legalising or encouraging suicide attempts but rather protecting the survivors.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide

sentences.text: Tinubu's proposal has been welcomed by Senate President Godswill Akpabio, who had previously suggested that people who survived suicide attempts should be sent to prison.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide

sentences.text: "We are saying that suicide is a crime for now.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide

sentences.text: Therefore, if you attempt it, we will send you to prison," Akpabio had said.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide

sentences.text: However, after receiving the Tinubu's proposal, he sought to clarify his earlier remarks, saying they did not apply to people experiencing mental health conditions.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide

sentences.text: He added that punishing people whose actions were influenced by mental health conditions would be insensitive.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide

sentences.text: Tinubu's letter follows sustained calls from mental health professionals for the law to be changed.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide

sentences.text: At a parliamentary public hearing in May 2024, the then president of the Association of Psychiatrists of Nigeria, Professor Taiwo Obindo, urged lawmakers to remove criminal penalties for attempted suicide.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide

sentences.text: "Why do we, as a nation, then punish individuals who are ill and need medical attention rather than prosecution?" he asked.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide

sentences.text: Drawing on his experience as a psychiatrist, Obindo said most people who die by suicide have a history of mental illness.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide

sentences.text: Akpabio has referred the president's amendment bill to the relevant senate committee for further consideration.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide

sentences.text: Nigeria is among several African countries where attempted suicide remains a criminal offence.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide

sentences.text: Ghana decriminalised attempted suicide in 2023, while Kenya's High Court ruled in January 2025 that the law criminalising it was unconstitutional.
sentences.article_title: Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide

sentences.text: The railway runs through Catumbela, near the Angolan city of Lobito, on the Atlantic coast.

sentences.text: But the railway has ambitions far bigger than improving local transport.
sentences.article_title: Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?

sentences.text: It is part of the Lobito Corridor, a US-backed effort to secure access to Africa's critical minerals and promote regional economic cooperation, which Washington hopes will help bring peace to conflict-torn eastern DR Congo.
sentences.article_title: Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?

sentences.text: Under agreements brokered by US President Donald Trump, DR Congo and neighbouring Rwanda have committed to greater economic cooperation, including more transparent mineral supply chains and regional infrastructure development.
sentences.article_title: Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?

sentences.text: The wider plan envisages linking these initiatives to the railway, which transports minerals from Central Africa to Western markets via Angola, rather than east to China as most do currently.
sentences.article_title: Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?

sentences.text: The hope is that formalising the mineral trade and encouraging investment could help curb illicit markets that have helped finance armed groups and fuel instability.
sentences.article_title: Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?

sentences.text: Manuela Julia says the railway has made travelling around easier But can a railway built to move minerals to global markets also deliver peace and prosperity?
sentences.article_title: Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?

sentences.text: The Lobito Corridor links DR Congo's mineral-rich south to Angola's Atlantic coast through the Benguela Railway and the Port of Lobito.
sentences.article_title: Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?

sentences.text: Its importance has grown as demand for copper and cobalt rises, driven partly by the global transition to cleaner energy, as both are critical ingredients for all kinds of electrical components.
sentences.article_title: Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?

sentences.text: The US sees the corridor as a means to diversify mineral supplies and reduce reliance on China, which dominates much of the world's processing capacity.
sentences.article_title: Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?

sentences.text: A US-DR Congo strategic partnership identifies the route from the Congolese town of Sakania to Lobito as a priority for mineral exports, while the economic framework agreed by DR Congo and Rwanda envisages connecting regional infrastructure and trade initiatives to the corridor.
sentences.article_title: Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?

sentences.text: The project has attracted over $750m (£570m), including funding backed by the US International Development Finance Corporation and the Development Bank of Southern Africa to upgrade railway tracks, signalling systems and trains.
sentences.article_title: Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?

sentences.text: The railway, built in 1902 under Portuguese colonial rule, was originally designed to transport goods and minerals from Central Africa to the Atlantic coast.
sentences.article_title: Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?

sentences.text: After years of disruption during Angola's civil war, it was rebuilt and fully reopened in 2015.
sentences.article_title: Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?

sentences.text: The US first got involved in the project under former President Joe Biden but backing has continued under Trump.
sentences.article_title: Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?

sentences.text: At Lobito's mineral terminal, the renewed ambitions are already visible.

sentences.article_title: Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?

sentences.article_title: Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?

sentences.text: The cargo is handled by Lobito Atlantic Railway (LAR), which has a 30-year concession to operate freight services along the corridor and manage the mineral terminal.

sentences.article_title: Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?

sentences.text: LAR expects to transport about 200,000 tonnes of copper through the corridor in 2026.

sentences.text: Nearly five years after the full-scale invasion of Ukraine turned him into a pariah, Putin is back on the global stage The meeting hasn't even happened yet.

sentences.text: Fast forward to 2026: Vladimir Putin has secured an historic meeting in Shenzhen.

sentences.text: For the first time in history, the leaders of China, Russia and the United States will sit down – just the three of them – for talks.
sentences.article_title: Steve Rosenberg: Historic talks with Xi and Trump are a coup for Putin

sentences.article_title: Steve Rosenberg: Historic talks with Xi and Trump are a coup for Putin

sentences.text: It allows him to boast that Western pressure on Russia has failed.
sentences.article_title: Steve Rosenberg: Historic talks with Xi and Trump are a coup for Putin

sentences.text: That was followed by a meeting with Xi Jinping.
sentences.article_title: Steve Rosenberg: Historic talks with Xi and Trump are a coup for Putin

sentences.article_title: Steve Rosenberg: Historic talks with Xi and Trump are a coup for Putin

sentences.text: It allows him to play global statesman, even as the Russian military continues to pound Ukrainian towns and cities, and the Kremlin continues to reject the idea of an unconditional, comprehensive ceasefire.
sentences.article_title: Steve Rosenberg: Historic talks with Xi and Trump are a coup for Putin

sentences.text: One short meeting is unlikely to reshape the world.
sentences.article_title: Steve Rosenberg: Historic talks with Xi and Trump are a coup for Putin

sentences.text: But it's the optics that are key.
sentences.article_title: Steve Rosenberg: Historic talks with Xi and Trump are a coup for Putin
