sentences.text: Shark Tank investor Kevin O'Leary is behind a major AI data centre project in Canada that has so far been embraced by legislators.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: As Americans have grown increasingly sour on artificial intelligence (AI) data centre development, Canada's industry leaders are sensing an opportunity.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: "Data centres in Canada looking pretty appealing right now," Lucy Hargreaves, CEO of non-profit policy group Build Canada, wrote on X the day after American voters passed 40 of 41 local ballot initiatives aimed at limiting or preventing data centre development in this month's midterm elections.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: While the number of proposed AI data centres in the US dwarfs that of its northern neighbour, in recent months Canada is being increasingly pitched as a hub for these so-called "hyperscale" projects.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: Those in favour argue that Canada's abundant land, natural gas and cold climate make it uniquely positioned to address some of the problems facing US AI infrastructure, from data centres' proximity to populated areas to noise pollution and strain on electricity grids.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: "Some of the capital that would have been deployed to build data centres in the US is now more available for Canada," Hargreaves told the BBC in an interview.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: "The question really is whether or not we want to go for that." Unlike in the US, pushback to these projects in Canada has been muted - at least so far.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: Many are going ahead without significant disruptions, and legislators have openly embraced them without major political consequences.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: At the heart of Canada's AI data centre boom is Alberta, where 90% of all currently proposed sites are set to be built.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: The western Canadian province, rich with natural gas deposits, has pitched itself as "North America's destination of choice" for AI data centres, including by offering a "concierge" service for investors to help build these projects at "unparalleled speed".
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: One of those investors is Kevin O'Leary, the Canadian businessman, TV personality and an ally of Donald Trump, who announced plans this year to build two large AI data centres - one in Alberta and one in the US state of Utah.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: His planned sites, both named Wonder Valley, are being received in very different ways on either side of the border.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: Residents in Utah have organised a fierce opposition campaign. , external The pushback led outgoing state senator Stuart Adams to demand in June that O'Leary scale down the project by 75% , external , from 40,000 to 13,000 acres.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: Financing for the Utah Wonder Valley data centre is still underway, and it is unclear when - and if - shovels will hit the ground on the project.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: The proposed 7,000-acre, 7.5-gigawatt Alberta Wonder Valley project, meanwhile, has received strong backing from both the provincial government and the local municipality.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: The project is billed as "off-grid" , external , relying on its own power system fuelled by natural gas sourced from the region.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: In April, the Alberta government exempted the project from an environmental impact assessment , external , arguing it was unnecessary, though it will still need to obtain permits prior to construction.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: The project was met with only limited opposition at a local town hall earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: One resident, Dan Harms, told Bloomberg in June , external that he saw the economic benefits of the Wonder Valley data centre and that it was being built "out in the middle of nowhere".
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: In an interview with BBC News, Reeve Ryan Ratzlaf, of Greenview Municipality in north-western Alberta, said the project was the "perfect fit" for his rural community, which had been looking for an industrial tenant to fill a resource-rich parcel of land for 13 years.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: Some community members have expressed concern about the amount of water needed to cool the proposed site annually, which is projected to be six million cubic metres, or about the size of 2,400 Olympic-size swimming pools.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: Ratzlaf argued the amount was a drop compared to the annual flow of the nearby Smoky River, from which the centre would pull water.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: More broadly, he said he believed that economic benefits to the region outweighed potential risks.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: "It's a giant warehouse with computer equipment inside," he said, arguing that it was less risky than petrochemical plants that could have been built in its place.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: Speaking to BBC News, the CEO overseeing both O'Leary projects, Paul Palandjian, said the two were proceeding at an "equal" pace.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: He acknowledged it had become more of a "hot topic" in the US than in Alberta.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: Sturgeon Lake Cree Nation has also recently sued the government over its decision to override the environmental assessment for O'Leary's Wonder Valley data centre, labelling it "irrational" in court filings.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: This week, the Alberta government proposed legislation that would put restrictions on where data centres could be built in a bid to ease some concerns.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: There are also signs that public cooperation may be fading elsewhere in the country.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: But experts say the US backlash offers a cautionary tale for Canada as it tries to capitalise on the AI boom.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: "AI is generally not very popular.

sentences.text: This is both true in Canada and the United States," noted Sean Mullin, a senior fellow at the University of Toronto and former adviser to Canada's prime minister on the national sovereign AI compute strategy.
